Se actualizan los datos sobre los mercados en el párrafo 7 y se añaden los comentarios de Bowman en los tres últimos párrafos

  • El IPC subyacente sube un 0,3 % en octubre por tercer mes consecutivo
  • El rendimiento de los bonos del Tesoro a dos años registra su mayor subida desde principios de abril de 2025
  • Logan afirma que es posible un ritmo más rápido de subidas de tipos; Waller señala la posibilidad de un movimiento de 50 puntos básicos
  • Los mercados apuestan por subidas de 25 puntos básicos en diciembre y enero si la Fed no sube los tipos en 50 puntos básicos el mes que viene

Por Howard Schneider y Ann Saphir

WASHINGTON, 10 nov (Reuters) - Las probabilidades de que la Reserva Federal suba los tipos de interés medio punto porcentual el próximo mes se dispararon el martes después de que los datos de EEUU mostraran que los precios subieron más rápido de lo esperado (link) en octubre y de que los responsables políticos dejaran la puerta abierta a un ritmo más rápido de subidas de tipos.

El índice de precios al consumo subió un 0,4 % en términos mensuales en octubre, por debajo del 0,6 % registrado en septiembre, a medida que remitía la inflación de la energía. Sin embargo, el índice subyacente —que excluye los precios volátiles de los alimentos y la energía— subió un 0,3 % por tercer mes consecutivo, lo que pone de manifiesto una inflación subyacente persistente y presiones sobre los precios que se extienden por toda la economía.

Unas horas antes de que se publicaran los datos, el gobernador de la Fed, Christopher Waller, afirmó que tenía previsto apoyar una subida de un cuarto de punto en la reunión de la Fed del 8 al 9 de diciembre, a menos que el IPC subyacente se situara en el 0,3 % o más.

«En ese caso, creo que debería considerarse una subida de 50 puntos básicos del tipo de interés oficial en la reunión de diciembre», afirmó en una conferencia celebrada en Londres y organizada por la King’s Business School y la Money Macro and Finance Society.

Waller señaló que limitarse a una subida de tipos más moderada supondría el riesgo de mermar la credibilidad de la Fed en la lucha contra la inflación, dado que esta era demasiado elevada y parecía estar generalizándose.

Los economistas encuestados por Reuters esperaban que la inflación subyacente mensual cayera al 0,2 % en octubre. Los datos del IPC y los comentarios de Waller provocaron una fuerte ola de ventas en el mercado de bonos del Tesoro de EEUU, y el rendimiento de los bonos a dos años —un indicador de las expectativas sobre la política de la Fed— registró su mayor subida desde principios de abril de 2025.

A media mañana, los precios del mercado reflejaban una probabilidad de alrededor del 15 % de que se produjera una subida de tipos de medio punto, antes de retroceder hasta aproximadamente el 10 % a última hora de la tarde. A lo largo del día, los operadores también apostaron masivamente por que la Fed mantendría sus habituales subidas de tipos de un cuarto de punto, pero que llevaría a cabo tres de ellas para mediados de 2027, en lugar de las dos previstas antes de conocerse los datos.

POSIBLE UN AVANCE MÁS RÁPIDO

La presidenta de la Fed de Dallas, Lorie Logan, afirmó en unas declaraciones separadas durante una conferencia sobre energía que «podría ser posible actuar con mayor rapidez» que el ritmo que implicaba la subida de un cuarto de punto porcentual aprobada en septiembre (link), seguida de una pausa en la siguiente reunión, en octubre. Logan señaló que, en su opinión, la Fed necesita subir los tipos al menos medio punto porcentual más antes de hacer una pausa para evaluar la situación.

«El objetivo debería ser que la política monetaria sea moderadamente restrictiva, de modo que podamos garantizar de forma sostenible tanto el máximo empleo como la estabilidad de los precios», afirmó Logan, señalando que el tipo de interés oficial actual, situado entre el 3,75 % y el 4,00 %, era demasiado bajo y «contribuía a las presiones inflacionistas».

El presidente de la Fed de Kansas City, Jeffrey Schmid, que organizó la conferencia junto con Logan, afirmó que la inflación es su «principal preocupación» y que él también cree que el tipo de interés oficial del banco central es «bastante acomodaticio». Pidió a los asistentes que se pusieran en la piel de los responsables de la política monetaria de la Fed y que indicaran si consideraban que la Fed debería recortar, mantener o subir los tipos en diciembre; ninguno optó por un recorte, y una amplia mayoría se decantó por una subida.

«¿No es eso bastante interesante? Y creo que, de hecho, resulta instructivo», afirmó, añadiendo que una parte importante de su trabajo consiste en desmitificar lo que hace la Fed, incluido el modo en que toma las decisiones sobre la fijación de tipos.

RIESGOS DE INFLACIÓN CONTINUADOS

Los datos de inflación de octubre se publicaron tras las elecciones de mitad de mandato en EEUU (link) de la semana pasada, que giraron en torno a cuestiones relacionadas con el coste de la vida y terminaron con un revés para el presidente Donald Trump (link) y su Partido Republicano.

Los datos de octubre mostraron subidas inesperadas en el coste de los seguros de automóvil, el transporte público y los servicios médicos, aumentos que podrían afectar con especial dureza a los hogares de ingresos medios y bajos. Los responsables políticos consideran que esos grupos son el eslabón débil en un panorama general sólido del gasto de los consumidores.

«No había mucho en el informe de hoy que disipara las preocupaciones sobre los riesgos de inflación actuales o sobre el hecho de que la Fed tendrá que subir aún más los tipos de interés para frenar las presiones sobre los precios», escribió Omair Sharif, presidente de Inflation Insights, tras la publicación de los datos del IPC.

Señaló que, según los datos, el índice de precios de los gastos de consumo personal (PCE) subyacente se encamina a subir un 0,34 % en octubre, lo que se traduciría en una tasa anualizada del 4 % y supondría un aumento con respecto al mes anterior. La Fed utiliza el índice de precios del PCE para medir los avances hacia su objetivo de inflación del 2 %, pero considera que la cifra subyacente es un mejor indicador de las tendencias inflacionistas.

La vicepresidenta de Supervisión de la Fed, Michelle Bowman, declaró más tarde el martes que ella también estaba preocupada por la inflación persistente, pero advirtió de que el endurecimiento de las condiciones financieras, debido a la caída de los precios de las acciones y al aumento de los rendimientos de los bonos, planteaba riesgos potenciales para la economía.

Afirmó que esperaba que la inflación se moderara el próximo año, siempre y cuando remitieran las presiones sobre los precios derivadas del auge de la inteligencia artificial y del conflicto en Oriente Medio, y no parecía tener prisa por subir los tipos de interés.

«La tendencia de la inflación no es a la baja, y creo que eso debería hacernos reflexionar a la hora de plantearnos la necesidad de abordar la inflación, así como el ritmo y el calendario para hacerlo», declaró Bowman en Washington, en el Consejo de Relaciones Exteriores. «Dejaré que las declaraciones de mis colegas hablen por sí mismas, pero sin duda creo que hoy he dado a entender que, en mi opinión, abordar la inflación es la medida adecuada para nosotros».

Updates markets in paragraph 7, adds Bowman comments in final three paragraphs

  • Core CPI rises 0.3% in October for third straight month
  • Yield on 2-year Treasury note posts biggest rise since early April 2025
  • Logan says more rapid rate-hike pace is possible; Waller flags chance of 50-basis-point move
  • Markets bet on 25-basis-point hikes in December and January if Fed does not raise by 50 basis points next month

By Howard Schneider and Ann Saphir

WASHINGTON, Nov 10 (Reuters) - The odds that the Federal Reserve may raise interest rates by half a percentage point next month jumped on Tuesday after US data showed prices rising faster than expected in October and policymakers opened the door to a quicker pace of rate hikes.

The Consumer Price Index rose 0.4% on a monthly basis in October, down from the 0.6% registered in September as energy inflation receded. The core index excluding volatile food and energy prices, however, rose 0.3% for the third month in a row, evidence of persistent underlying inflation and price pressures spreading through the economy.

A few hours before the data was released, Fed Governor Christopher Waller said he planned to support a quarter-point increase at the Fed's December 8-9 meeting unless core CPI came in at 0.3% or more.

"In that case, I believe a 50-basis-point hike in the policy rate should be considered at the December meeting," he said at a conference in London hosted by King's Business School and the Money Macro and Finance Society.

Sticking with a smaller rate increase, Waller said, risked hurting the Fed's inflation-fighting credibility, given inflation was too high and appeared to be broadening.

Economists polled by Reuters had expected core monthly inflation to drop to 0.2% in October. The CPI data and Waller's comments drove a powerful selloff in the US Treasury market, with the yield on 2-year notes — a proxy for Fed policy expectations — rising by the most since early April 2025.

By mid-morning, market pricing reflected about a 15% chance of a half-point rate hike before retreating to about 10% in the late afternoon. Over the course of the day, traders also piled into bets the Fed would keep to its usual quarter-point rate hikes but deliver three of them by mid-2027, rather than two as seen before the data.

MORE RAPID MOVE POSSIBLE

Dallas Fed President Lorie Logan said in separate remarks at an energy conference that it "may be possible to move more rapidly" than the pace implied by the quarter-percentage-point hike approved in September followed by a hold at the following meeting, in October. Logan said she feels the Fed needs to raise rates by at least half a percentage point more before pausing to take stock.

"The goal should be to make policy modestly restrictive so we can sustainably deliver both maximum employment and stable prices," Logan said, noting that the current 3.75%-4.00% policy rate was too low and "adding to inflationary pressures."

Kansas City Fed President Jeffrey Schmid, who hosted the conference with Logan, said inflation is "top of mind" for him and that he too believes the central bank's policy rate is "fairly accommodative." He asked attendees to think of themselves as Fed policymakers and to indicate whether they felt the Fed should cut, hold steady or raise rates in December; none picked a cut, and a large majority picked a hike.

"Isn't that kind of interesting? And I think it's actually instructive," he said, adding that a big part of his job is to demystify what the Fed does, including how it makes rate-setting decisions.

ONGOING INFLATION RISKS

The October inflation data followed US midterm elections last week that revolved around cost-of-living issues and ended in a rebuke of President Donald Trump and his Republican Party.

The October data showed unexpected jumps in the cost of auto insurance, public transportation and medical services, increases that could land particularly hard on middle- and lower-income households. Policymakers see those groups as the weak link in an overall solid consumer spending picture.

"There was not much in today's report to assuage concerns about ongoing inflation risks or the fact that the Fed will need to hike rates further to tamp down price pressures," Omair Sharif, president of Inflation Insights, wrote after the release of the CPI data.

He said the data put the core Personal Consumption Expenditures Price Index on track to rise 0.34% in October, which would translate into a 4% annualized pace and represent an increase from the prior month. The Fed uses the PCE Price Index to measure progress toward its 2% inflation target, but it considers the core figure a better measure of inflation trends.

Fed Vice Chair for Supervision Michelle Bowman said later on Tuesday that she too was worried about persistent inflation, but warned that tighter financial conditions from falling stock prices and higher bond yields posed potential risks to the economy.

She said she expected inflation to cool next year as long as price pressures from the AI buildout and the Middle East conflict abate, and did not sound in a hurry about rate hikes.

"The trend is not on a downward trend for inflation, and I think that that should give us some pause as we think about the need to address inflation and at what pace and on what timeline," Bowman said in Washington at the Council on Foreign Relations. "I would let my colleagues' statements speak for themselves, but certainly I think I gave an indication today that I think addressing inflation is the right move for us."

(Reporting by Howard Schneider and Ann Saphir; Editing by Andrea Ricci, Paul Simao and Jamie Freed)

(( howard.schneider@tr.com ))

"Upgrading of Highly Paraffinic Crude Oil By Conversion of Hydrocarbon Compounds Having Substantially Saturated Chains to Lower-Molecular-Weight Hydrocarbons" in Patent Application Approval Process (USPTO 20260327500)

2026 NOV 10-- By a News Reporter-Staff News Editor at Chemicals& Chemistry Business Daily Business Daily Daily-- A patent application by the inventors Adhikari, Birendra; Jhawar, Anil K.; Trygstad, W Marcus, filed on April 22, 2026, was made available online on October 22, 2026, according to news reporting originating from Washington, D.C., by NewsRx correspondents. 2026 NOV 10 (NewsRx) -- By a News Reporter-Staff News Editor at Chemicals & Chemistry Business Daily Business Daily Daily -- A patent application by the inventors Adhikari, Birendra (Sarnia, CA); Jhawar, Anil K. (London, CA); Trygstad, W Marcus (Spring, TX, US), filed on April 22, 2026, was made available online on October 22, 2026, according to news reporting originating from Washington, D.C., by NewsRx correspondents.

This patent application has not been assigned to a company or institution.

The following quote was obtained by the news editors from the background information supplied by the inventors: "

"Technical Field

"This invention relates to hydrocarbon processing, and more particularly to systems and methods for efficiently producing high value products such as transportation fuels and chemical feedstocks.

"Background Information

"Throughout this application, various publications, patents and published patent applications are referred to by an identifying citation. The disclosures of the publications, patents and published patent applications referenced in this application are hereby incorporated by reference into the present disclosure.

"Thermolytic Methods

The thermolytic methods are practiced under various rubrics including pyrolysis and hydrothermal liquefaction, where the latter may be more aptly described as supercritical-water pyrolysis (SCWP) due to its application of water at temperatures and pressures well above its supercritical point and in quantities that are mass-multiples versus feedstock. Because the instant invention is not pyrolytic, it substantially avoids numerous problems inherent in the operation of thermolytic mechanisms for chemical recycling of waste plastic. The first relates to their general lack of selectivity. In what is effectively thermal cracking, thermolytic methods rely on the input of thermal energy to rupture bonds in polymer compounds. When these are saturated polyalkylenes, bonds ruptured include both carbon-carbon bonds (C-C) in the polymer skeleton and the associated carbon-hydrogen bonds (C-H). Occurrence of the latter on adjacent carbons is thermolytic dehydrogenation that yields unsaturations, e.g., carbon-carbon double bonds (C═C), which are alkene groups. The rupturing of C-C ostensibly creates reactive free radical intermediates. Numerous secondary reactions ensue, which generate products with diverse molecular weights and structure. Moreover, in what may be aptly described as carbon scrambling, the many reactions result in wholesale rearrangement of hydrocarbon functionalities native to the polymer chains and the proliferation of non-native functionalities. Thus, the product from thermolytic methods comprises compounds with a wide range of molecular weights and highly diverse structures and chemical functionality. The lack of selectivity has a further consequence of limiting possibilities to control production of both light hydrocarbon gases and heavy, carbonaceous char, which together compromise overall yields of useful hydrocarbons.

"A second feature relates to the first: the rate dependency of thermolytic mechanisms and process throughput on elevated process temperatures, which commonly are at/above 440 °C, makes them highly energy-intensive. Third, each occurrence of carbon-carbon bond rupturing or thermolytic dehydrogenation generates one unsaturation in product compounds. Even saturated naphthenic structures formed through carbon scrambling are understood in organic chemistry to represent unsaturations. In the hydrocarbon processing industry, alkene functionality is often problematic: it renders fuels unstable and causes coking in naphtha crackers. Although the product from SCWP is touted as having lower C═C content than that from conventional pyrolysis, which is nominally anhydrous, levels are nonetheless relatively high; products from all thermolytic methods typically must be stabilized and upgraded by post-processing, e.g., by hydrotreating.

"A fourth problem is a direct consequence of the first and third: alkene functionality formed by dehydrogenation is itself an agent of functionality proliferation in the reaction mixture, as it is predisposed to form (i) allylic intermediates and (ii) conjugated dienes through further dehydrogenation. Both may undergo diverse addition reactions known to skilled artisans including ones leading to formation of aromatic functionality.

"A notable, fifth issue in the application of thermolytic methods for chemical recycling of PO relates to the aforementioned scrambling of functionality that ensues after generation of free-radical intermediates. Non-polyalkylene contaminants in waste plastic feedstocks commonly include (i) polymers such as polyamides (nylons), polyesters (e.g., poly(ethylene terephthalate) esters, or PET), polyurethanes, and poly(vinylchloride), or PVC; (ii) additives that are compounded into the polyalkylenes for-use, e.g., fillers, colorants, plasticizers, and lubricants that facilitate molding or extrusion; and (iii) and miscellaneous other materials, e.g., paper. Most such contaminants contain heteroatoms, e.g., nitrogen, oxygen, and chlorine, which may become covalently integrated into product compounds through the uncontrolled side reactions involving free radicals. As with alkenes, heteroatom-containing functionalities may be substantially eliminated by post-processing techniques such as hydrotreating, which is readily available in the context of petroleum refining. Yet, such techniques do not come without cost or conditions. For example, the pyrolytic processing of polyolefinic waste plastic may be effective when integrated with petroleum refining operations but its economic relevance is constrained apart from such infrastructure. Nevertheless, the incorporation of heteroatoms from contaminants into thermolytic products represents a sixth problem with thermolytic methods applied for chemical recycling of waste plastic: the requirement to source feedstocks whose PO content typically is greater than about 95%. Although plastic sorting technologies can do this, they should be understood as producing such PO-enriched waste plastic streams at the expense of rejecting other fractions that contain lower levels of PO, e.g., <90%, and correspondingly higher levels of the aforementioned contaminants. This proportionately diminishes the total amount of PO-containing feedstocks available for chemical recycling by pyrolysis relative to total PO in the waste plastic; and it in turn increases the cost of the high-PO pyrolysis feedstocks, not only because of the low yield per tonne of waste plastic, but the additional cost incurred to dispose of the rejected lower-PO fraction.

"A need therefore exists for addressing the aforementioned drawbacks of the prior art."

Oct 27, 2026: Southern Copper's Growth Prospects Clouded by Tia Maria Delays

Southern Copper Corporation (NYSE:SCCO) is navigating a complex landscape of robust earnings juxtaposed with project delays, particularly concerning its Tia Maria project in Peru. On the 27th of October 2026, the company reported record third-quarter revenue, adjusted EBITDA, and net earnings, enhanced by higher copper prices and strong contributions from its Mexican operations.

Despite these impressive figures, the company faces challenges due to falling copper prices and lower ore grades at its Peruvian mines. Southern Copper's production from its Toquepala and Cuajone mines has reportedly declined, necessitating increased output from its Mexican operations to maintain overall production levels. The delays at Tia Maria, where construction has been postponed to accommodate additional engineering work, add another layer of complexity to the company's growth outlook.

Southern Copper's successful quarter was largely driven by price increases rather than volume growth, raising concerns about the sustainability of such earnings in the face of fluctuating commodity prices. Management emphasized that while Mexican operations provided a necessary buffer, the ongoing issues in Peru must be addressed to ensure long-term stability. The company has a diverse asset base, operating across Mexico and Peru, but the current focus remains on overcoming the challenges posed by its Peruvian projects.

Looking ahead, the company has ambitious plans for growth, including a decade-long capital program aimed at increasing annual copper output. Projects like El Pilar in Mexico are set to advance, but uncertainties surrounding community relations, regulatory approvals, and production execution in Peru remain critical to Southern Copper's future performance. The market eagerly awaits updates on these initiatives, particularly the long-stalled Tia Maria project, which holds significant potential for enhancing the company's production capacity once operational.

Investors are advised to monitor Southern Copper's performance closely, as the interplay between copper prices, production volumes, and project timelines will play a pivotal role in shaping the company's trajectory. Record earnings provide a strong foundation, but the ability to manage the challenges posed by project delays and fluctuating market conditions will ultimately determine Southern Copper's growth and sustainability.

Recent News 2 of 9, Source: HourlyBusinessNews

Oct 26, 2026: Southern Copper Corporation Considers $968 Million Cuajone Expansion

Southern Copper Corporation is contemplating a significant expansion of its Cuajone copper mine in southern Peru, with a proposed investment of $968 million. The company announced on 28th October 2026 that the expansion would aim to increase milling capacity by 33%, from the current 90,000 tonnes per day to 120,000 tonnes per day.

Southern Copper's expansion plans would necessitate additional mining equipment and the establishment of a new production line at the Cuajone concentrator. The company estimates that the expanded operations could yield an average of 55,000 tonnes of copper and 1,400 tonnes of molybdenum annually, bolstering its output amidst current production challenges.

In addition to the immediate $968 million expansion plan, Southern Copper is exploring a larger scale enhancement that could increase milling capacity to 150,000 tonnes per day. CEO Raul Jacob indicated that while both options are under consideration, the 120,000-tonne-per-day scenario is currently deemed more feasible. A decision regarding the expansion's scale is expected in early 2027.

Despite these ambitious plans, Southern Copper has yet to finalize an investment decision or outline a specific construction timetable. The proposal comes at a time when the company faces challenges related to lower ore grades affecting its Peruvian operations, with mined copper production declining by 2.9% to 693,602 tonnes during the first nine months of 2026, primarily due to diminished grades at its mines in the region.

Cuajone serves as an open-pit copper and molybdenum operation located in Peru's Moquegua region. Southern Copper Corporation, which operates several mines and metallurgical facilities in both Peru and Mexico, is primarily owned by Grupo Mexico, holding an 88.9% stake in the company.

Oct 13, 2026: Southern Copper Corporation Targets US$471 Million Investment at Toquepala

Southern Copper Corporation is poised to invest US$471 million in significant upgrades to enhance efficiency and ensure the operational continuity of its Toquepala mine in Peru. This investment is part of the company's broader strategy to bolster its mining operations in the region. The announcement was made on 14th October 2026, highlighting the company's commitment to maintaining productivity and sustainability in its mining activities.

The planned improvements will primarily focus on increasing the storage capacity of the Quebrada Honda tailings deposit, alongside enabling new operational areas. According to the modification plan submitted to the environmental certifier Senace, the tailings deposit elevation will be raised from 1,246.5 to 1,256.5 meters above sea level. This expansion will also involve enhancing the East waste dump capacity, augmenting auxiliary facilities in Concentrator Plant 2, and implementing a domestic wastewater treatment plant for the Villa Staff camp, among other critical actions.

SAO PAULO, Nov 10 (Reuters) - The Brazilian government is set to present a bill this week with measures that aim to achieve a fiscal adjustment equivalent to 0.5% of gross domestic product in 2027, news outlet G1 reported on Tuesday.

Among the measures are the exclusion of extraordinary revenues from the basis for calculation of the constitutional spending floors for health and education, it added, citing sources close to President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva.

(Reporting by Andre Romani in Sao Paulo; Editing by Chris Reese)

New Science Findings from University of los Andes Described (Partisan politics and stock returns under strong presidential regimes: Religion and politics)

2026 NOV 10-- By a News Reporter-Staff News Editor at Politics, Law& Government Daily-- Research findings on Science are discussed in a new report. Using firm-level data, we show that the widely documented Democratic Party premium in the United States does not extend to this setting.". For more information on this research see: Partisan politics and stock returns... 2026 NOV 10 (NewsRx) -- By a News Reporter-Staff News Editor at Politics, Law & Government Daily -- Research findings on Science are discussed in a new report. According to news reporting out of Santiago, Chile, by NewsRx editors, the research stated, "This study examines how partisan politics affects stock returns in Latin American countries characterized by strong presidential regimes. Using firm-level data, we show that the widely documented Democratic Party premium in the United States does not extend to this setting."

Our news journalists obtained a quote from the research from the University of los Andes, "Instead, stock returns are highest under centrist governments, while elections won by left-wing candidates trigger negative market reactions. Beyond the traditional left-right dimension, we introduce a novel religious classification of political parties. We find that markets perform significantly better when presidents are affiliated with Christian parties, with higher average returns and positive abnormal returns following electoral victories. These effects are accompanied by lower measures of risk and higher profitability, suggesting that the superior performance is not driven by risk premium but rather by improved expected cash flows and market underreaction to political outcomes. Overall, the results indicate that partisan effects on stock returns depend on institutional context and extend beyond the conventional ideological spectrum."

According to the news editors, the research concluded: "The findings highlight the economic relevance of political religiosity and provide new evidence that financial markets respond systematically to political characteristics in strong presidential systems."

For more information on this research see: Partisan politics and stock returns under strong presidential regimes: Religion and politics. PLOS ONE , 2026;21(10). PLOS ONE can be contacted at: Public Library Science, 1160 Battery Street, Ste 100, San Francisco, CA 94111, USA. (Public Library of Science - www.plos.org ; PLOS ONE - www.plosone.org )

Our news journalists report that additional information may be obtained by contacting Javier Mella, University of los Andes, Santiago, Chile.

Peru raised US$4.5 billion today from the global financial market by issuing two bonds maturing in 12 and 30 years , funds which will be used for infrastructure projects aimed at adapting to climate change and managing disaster risk, as well as financing "programs and projects aimed at reducing social gaps, strengthening the protection of the most vulnerable populations, and fostering a more inclusive and sustainable economic growth," as announced.

This was achieved after receiving purchase offers from the market totaling over US$21 billion, a level of demand that allowed it to obtain the resources at annual rates of 6.06% and 6.45%, respectively, for each term in an operation managed by Citigroup, Crédit Agricole CIB, Deutsche Bank Securities, and Santander.

Moreover, it created conditions that allowed for a reduction in the initial spread of the UST + 160 basis points—on both maturities—to a spread of 42 basis points in the first tranche and 40 in the 30-year tranche. "This meant a negative new issue premium (12 years) and no premium (30 years)," explained Elmer Cuba, the Minister of Economy and Finance, when announcing the operation.

The issuance comes at a time of significant volatility in international markets, driven by the impact of conflicts on commodity prices and uncertainty regarding future interest rate movements, but it simultaneously confirms that this has not dampened global appetite for so-called "emerging market risk."

At the same time, it exposes the ongoing financial isolation of Argentina, even as the country reports fiscal, trade, and current account surpluses—while beginning to recover reserves—which will compel the Government to reformulate its financial program for the coming year, given that recent months have seen a tightening of the local market for dollar placements, due to the significant gap that has opened between bonds maturing before and after the end of the Milei administration's term.

Looking from the Outside

Market concern, analysts agree, is understandable. The Government, which had to pause the remaining issuance of nearly US$800 million from the Bonar 2029 (AO29) to avoid validating rates higher than 15% annually, had planned to raise US$5 billion through local issuances next year according to the program presented mid-year to provide market predictability.

In light of current circumstances, this potential shortfall is noticeable, leading the market to await possible definitive announcements from alternative sources. However, repeated inquiries by LA NACION to the Ministry of Economy regarding a possible reformulation of this plan went unanswered.

"Between January, July, and October 2027, there are Bonar and Global maturities totaling US$12.242 billion (US$4.553 billion in January, US$5.663 billion in July, and US$2.026 billion in October). In addition to these obligations, there is an external asset formation averaging US$2.4 billion per month, which could intensify with electoral uncertainty (it reached US$6.8 billion in September 2025)," noted analyst Nery Persichini from GMA, explaining the market's distrust, reflected in a risk rate that recently exceeded 900 points (though it is now below that level) and the spreads of between 12 and 15 points that have emerged between the A027 bond (which matures before the presidential election) and the AO28 and AO29 bonds.

Additionally, he noted that prices for credit default swaps (CDS) indicate that the implied probability of default on Argentine debt over five years soared to 51%, up from 29% in June, while the probability over ten years reached 73% compared to 52% mid-year, both at their highest levels since the spike of September 2025, when they were 68% and 86%, respectively. In the shorter term, the implied default probability for one year stands at 8%, still within limited absolute levels, although it has quadrupled from the 2% recorded in June.

"The 2027 elections and the continuation of the economic program are becoming increasingly significant in the valuations of Argentine assets. The market is beginning to look beyond the immediate situation and to implicitly price in doubts about the political support necessary to maintain the current course," observers from Portfolio Personal Inversiones (PPI) agree.

Unfazed by these issues, Peru demonstrated that access to the global debt market remains open, completing the largest sustainable bond issuance in dollars in its history and following a program approved last May.

In parallel, it launched a swap offer for its global dollar bonds maturing in 2027, 2030, and 2031, for new securities maturing in 2038, aiming to "improve the profile of public debt and strengthen the long-term references of the foreign currency yield curve."

Candidate Rubén Quispe Capajaña, from the Somos Perú party, has been declared the elected mayor of the Conima district following a coin toss.

The decision was made by the Special Electoral Jury (JEE) of Huancané due to an unprecedented tie of 671 votes against his opponent in the municipal elections.

According to the official figures from the National Office of Electoral Processes (ONPE), with 100% of the ballots counted, both Rubén Quispe Capajaña and Salomino Mamani Quispe, candidate for País Para Todos, received exactly 27.739% of the valid votes.

Given the impossibility of breaking the tie at the polls, the electoral authorities called for a public hearing to determine the winner through a drawing.

The procedure began with the selection of the order among the representatives of both political groups. The candidate from Somos Perú won the right to choose first among five one-sol coins prepared for the event and opted for the "seal" side.

Subsequently, the president of the JEE of Huancané tossed the coin, resulting in a victory for Quispe Capajaña.

The mechanism used is legally supported. Paragraph 6 of Article 26 of the Municipal Elections Law (Law No. 26864) stipulates that in the event of a tie between two or more candidates for mayor, the winner must be determined through a drawing in a public act.

Following the drawing, the responses of both candidates highlighted the contrasting sentiments of the day. Quispe expressed his confidence in the process prior to the JEE's resolution.

On the opposite side, Salomino Mamani voiced his disagreement with the random mechanism and suggested the need to amend national legislation to incorporate a second electoral round in cases of ties.

Southern Copper Corporation (NYSE:SCCO) is a leading integrated copper producer, renowned for its extensive copper mining operations and low-cost production capabilities. Core activities encompass large-scale copper mining, smelting, and refining through key assets like the Toquepala and Cuajone mines, alongside Mexico's strategic copper operations. The company excels in producing copper concentrates and cathodes, while also generating molybdenum and silver byproducts. Southern Copper sustains its competitive edge through significant copper reserves, supporting industrial copper supply and expansion projects. Emphasizing sustainability, the company adopts innovative mining practices and maintains robust supply chain management, positioning itself to leverage long-term trends in electric vehicles and base metals demand.

Southern Copper Corporation, a New York Stock Exchange-listed company, is a leading global producer of copper and other metals, with operations centered in Mexico and Peru. • Los legisladores quieren reuniones informativas con Huang y las agencias de inteligencia
  • Schumer y Moolenaar afirman que esta cuestión obliga al Congreso a aprobar rápidamente nuevas restricciones a las exportaciones de chips estadounidenses a China
  • Schumer afirma que Trump debe explicar su defensa de Huang

Se añade información sobre la legislación en los párrafos 1-3, sobre Moolenaar en el párrafo 4 y sobre Guthrie en el párrafo 9

Por David Shepardson y Courtney Rozen

WASHINGTON, 10 nov (Reuters) - Los legisladores estadounidenses renovaron este martes sus llamamientos para que se impongan restricciones más estrictas al acceso de China a los chips avanzados de IA, después de que las acusaciones sobre los vínculos del director ejecutivo de Nvidia, Jensen Huang, con un espía chino intensificaran el escrutinio sobre el principal fabricante mundial de chips de IA.

Esta iniciativa refuerza los esfuerzos del Congreso por endurecer los controles de exportación de una tecnología fundamental para el desarrollo de la IA.

Estados Unidos y China compiten por crear modelos de IA superiores, y las autoridades estadounidenses llevan años intentando limitar el acceso de China a los chips de Nvidia para frenar el progreso de ese país. Según el *New York Times*, Huang está acusado de mantener una relación sentimental con una espía china, lo que ha llevado a los legisladores a pedir restricciones más estrictas al acceso de China a los chips de la empresa.

El líder demócrata del Senado, Chuck Schumer, instó el martes al Congreso a aprobar la «AI Overwatch Act», que otorgaría al Congreso competencias sobre las exportaciones de chips avanzados; la «Chip Security Act», que obligaría a las empresas a realizar un seguimiento de sus chips para combatir el contrabando; y la «Match Act», que presionaría a los aliados de EEUU para que restrinjan el envío de más equipos de fabricación de chips a China.

El presidente del Comité de China de la Cámara de Representantes, John Moolenaar, del Partido Republicano, afirmó en un comunicado que las restricciones a la exportación de chips deberían incluirse en el proyecto de ley anual de gasto militar de EEUU. Esta amplia legislación determina todo, desde el número de buques, aviones y sistemas de misiles que se adquieren, hasta el aumento salarial de las tropas y la forma de abordar las amenazas geopolíticas.

Schumer también afirmó que el Congreso debe obtener una explicación detallada sobre la defensa que el presidente Donald Trump ha hecho de Huang.

«Se supone que debe proteger a Estados Unidos, no a China, ni a sus amigos. Trump se ha dedicado a intentar defender a Jensen Huang cuando debería estar defendiendo nuestra seguridad nacional», afirmó Schumer.

Trump declaró el lunes (link) que el FBI estaba investigando las acusaciones de que Huang mantenía una relación con un espía chino, y afirmó que le apoya. Huang es uno de los aliados más cercanos de Trump (link) en Silicon Valley, y la relación entre ambos se remonta al menos a 2025.

En los últimos dos años, Huang ha expresado en repetidas ocasiones su apoyo a la agenda del Gobierno y se ha convertido en una presencia habitual en Washington, mientras Nvidia intentaba vender chips avanzados al mercado chino. Ha admitido haber mantenido una relación extramatrimonial. Nvidia afirma que, aunque su consejo de administración no tiene motivos para creer que se haya visto comprometida ni la seguridad nacional de EEUU ni los secretos de Nvidia, su investigación examinará toda la información disponible.

El presidente de la Comisión de Energía y Comercio de la Cámara de Representantes, Brett Guthrie, que está ayudando a dar forma a la agenda republicana en materia de IA, declaró el martes a Reuters que, cuando la investigación del FBI «avance, estoy seguro de que nuestra comisión tendrá que actuar».

Ni la Casa Blanca ni Nvidia respondieron de inmediato a las solicitudes de comentarios sobre la legislación.

La versión del Senado del proyecto de ley de defensa incluye la legislación que apoyan Schumer y Moolenaar.

Los legisladores también quieren que Huang responda a sus preguntas sobre las acusaciones relativas a su relación y sobre lo que Trump sabía al respecto.

Schumer citó informes según los cuales Trump fue informado hace un año de la relación de Huang con una presunta espía china y no hizo nada al respecto.

«Una de nuestras empresas más importantes, dedicada a la seguridad nacional, cuyo director ejecutivo podría estar manteniendo una relación con una espía china, y Trump no hizo nada al respecto», afirmó Schumer.

El senador demócrata Rubén Gallego señaló: «Nvidia ha estado solicitando permiso para vender chips avanzados a China. Necesitamos saber hasta qué punto la espía china influyó en la decisión del director ejecutivo Jensen».

• Lawmakers want briefings with Huang, intelligence agencies
  • Schumer, Moolenaar say issue means Congress must quickly pass new restrictions on US chips exports to China
  • Schumer says Trump must explain defense of Huang

Adds legislation in paragraphs 1-3, Moolenaar in paragraph 4, Guthrie in paragraph 9

By David Shepardson and Courtney Rozen

WASHINGTON, Nov 10 (Reuters) - US lawmakers on Tuesday renewed calls for tighter restrictions on China's access to advanced AI chips, after allegations about Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's ties to a Chinese spy intensified scrutiny of the world's leading AI chipmaker.

The push boosts congressional efforts to strengthen export controls on a technology that is critical to AI development.

The US and China are racing to build superior AI models, and US officials for years have tried to limit China's access to Nvidia's chips to slow the country's progress. Huang is accused of having a romantic relationship with a Chinese spy, according to the New York Times, prompting lawmakers to call for stronger restrictions on China's access to the company's chips.

Senate Democratic Leader Chuck Schumer on Tuesday called on Congress to pass the AI Overwatch Act, which would give Congress power over advanced chip exports, the Chip Security Act, which would require businesses to track their chips to combat smuggling, and the Match Act, which ⁠would push US allies to restrict sending more chipmaking equipment to China.

House China Committee Chairman John Moolenaar, a Republican, said in a statement that restrictions on chip exports should be included in the US's annual military spending bill. The sweeping legislation determines everything from how many ships, aircraft and missile systems are bought, to a pay raise for the troops, to how to address geopolitical threats.

Schumer also said Congress must have a full accounting of President Donald Trump's defense of Huang.

"He’s supposed to protect America, not China, not his friends. Trump has been busy trying to defend Jensen Huang when he ought to be defending our national security," Schumer said.

Trump on Monday said the FBI was looking into allegations that Huang had a relationship with a Chinese spy, and said he supports him. Huang is one of Trump's closest allies in Silicon Valley, and the relationship between the two dates ⁠to at least 2025.

Over the past two years, Huang has repeatedly voiced support for the administration's agenda and become ⁠a regular presence in Washington as Nvidia sought to sell advanced chips to the Chinese market. He has admitted to having an affair. Nvidia says that while its board has no reason to believe that either US national security or Nvidia secrets were compromised, its inquiry will examine all available information.

House Energy and Commerce Committee Chairman Brett Guthrie, who is helping shape Republicans' AI agenda, told Reuters on Tuesday that when the FBI investigation "moves forward, I'm sure our committee is going to have to act."

The White House and Nvidia did not immediately respond to requests for comment about the legislation.

A Senate version of the defense bill contains the legislation that Schumer and Moolenaar support.

Lawmakers also want Huang to answer their questions about the accusations about Huang's relationship, and what Trump knew about it.

Schumer cited reports Trump was briefed on Huang’s relationship with a suspected Chinese spy a year ago and did nothing.

"One of our most important companies that is involved in national security, and the CEO might be having an affair with a Chinese spy, and Trump did nothing about it," Schumer said.

Democratic Senator Ruben Gallego said, "Nvidia has been asking permission to sell advanced chips to China. We need to know how much the Chinese spy influenced CEO Jensen’s decision."

(Reporting by David Shepardson and Courtney Rozen in Washington; Additional reporting by Karen Freifeld in New York and Alexandra Alper in Washington; Editing by Alistair Bell)

US EQUITIES CLOSE LOWER WITH INFLATION BOOSTING BETS ON RATE HIKES

Wall Street's three major indexes finished lower with the Nasdaq Composite .IXIC leading declines, off 0.7%, as investors braced themselves for more aggressive tightening from the Federal Reserve after October's consumer inflation report showed that prices are still elevated.

Tuesday's decline in oil prices to two-month lows offered some support. But investors were mostly worried about stubborn inflation and the prospects for higher interest rates with commentary from Fed officials solidifying those concerns.

Traders were last betting on a 9.5% probability that the Fed would raise rates by half a percentage point in December compared with zero bets for this size of a hike before the inflation data, released before market open on Tuesday, according to the latest data from CME Group's FedWatch tool. The odds for a quarter-percentage-point increase in rates rose to 90.5% from 84% on Monday. And lastly traders saw zero chance that the Fed would keep rates where they are (3.75%-4.00% range) after the meeting, down from 16% on Monday.

Fed officials also helped dispel any remaining doubt in investors' minds that the odds for a hike had changed.

Dallas Federal Reserve President Lorie Logan said the US central bank needs to deliver at least two more quarter-percentage-point interest rate increases to bring down inflation, and may need to do so promptly to keep broadening price pressures from getting baked into the economy.

Kansas City Federal Reserve President Jeff Schmid said that inflation is "top of mind" as he signaled support for tightening policy to bring it under control, saying that he didn't think interest rates were restrictive last year, and that he believes "today it's fairly accommodative."

And hours before the data was released, Fed Governor Chris Waller had said that the Fed will need to take more aggressive monetary policy action if inflation continues to move away from its target.

Meanwhile, a report from the Federal Reserve Bank of New York said on Tuesday that the overall level of troubled borrowing in the US economy rose modestly in the third quarter but did not appear to signal a notable deterioration in credit quality.

Still. the indexes did manage to close above their session lows. And while the heavyweight technology sector .SPLRCT fell 1.4% and was the biggest drag on the S&P 500, five of the benchmark's 11 major sectors managed to close higher with financials' .SPSY 0.5% advance leading the charge.

Wall Street's three major indexes finished lower with the Nasdaq Composite .IXIC leading declines, off 0.7%, as investors braced themselves for more aggressive tightening from the Federal Reserve after October's consumer inflation report showed that prices are still elevated.

Tuesday's decline in oil prices to two-month lows offered some support. But investors were mostly worried about stubborn inflation and the prospects for higher interest rates with commentary from Fed officials solidifying those concerns.

Traders were last betting on a 9.5% probability that the Fed would raise rates by half a percentage point in December compared with zero bets for this size of a hike before the inflation data, released before market open on Tuesday, according to the latest data from CME Group's FedWatch tool. The odds for a quarter-percentage-point increase in rates rose to 90.5% from 84% on Monday. And lastly traders saw zero chance that the Fed would keep rates where they are (3.75%-4.00% range) after the meeting, down from 16% on Monday.

Fed officials also helped dispel any remaining doubt in investors' minds that the odds for a hike had changed.

Dallas Federal Reserve President Lorie Logan said the US central bank needs to deliver at least two more quarter-percentage-point interest rate increases to bring down inflation, and may need to do so promptly to keep broadening price pressures from getting baked into the economy.

Kansas City Federal Reserve President Jeff Schmid said that inflation is "top of mind" as he signaled support for tightening policy to bring it under control, saying that he didn't think interest rates were restrictive last year, and that he believes "today it's fairly accommodative."

And hours before the data was released, Fed Governor Chris Waller had said that the Fed will need to take more aggressive monetary policy action if inflation continues to move away from its target.

Meanwhile, a report from the Federal Reserve Bank of New York said on Tuesday that the overall level of troubled borrowing in the US economy rose modestly in the third quarter but did not appear to signal a notable deterioration in credit quality.

Still. the indexes did manage to close above their session lows. And while the heavyweight technology sector .SPLRCT fell 1.4% and was the biggest drag on the S&P 500, five of the benchmark's 11 major sectors managed to close higher with financials' .SPSY 0.5% advance leading the charge.

"I think first we would have to see those risks being abated before I would be confident in my expectations for next year," Bowman said at the Council on Foreign Relations. "With the status of the labor market the way that it is and conditions as they have stabilized since last fall, I think we should be shifting our focus, or I certainly am shifting my focus, to inflation."

CIUDAD DE MÉXICO, 10 nov (Reuters) - El peso mexicano se depreció el martes arrastrado por un avance global del dólar tras la divulgación de datos de inflación estadounidenses mayores a lo esperado, mientras que la bolsa se mantuvo oscilando en torno a su máximo histórico de 72,227 puntos.

El reporte reforzó las apuestas a que la Reserva Federal mantendrá una postura más restrictiva, luego de que autoridades del banco central estadounidense dejaron abierta la posibilidad de elevar, incluso, en medio punto porcentual las tasas de interés en su próxima reunión de diciembre.

* La moneda local MXN= cotizaba en 18.6292 unidades en la recta final de los negocios, con un retroceso de un 0.55%, después de dos jornadas de ganancias.

* "La expectativa de una Fed más restrictiva podría limitar el espacio de Banco de México para continuar normalizando su política monetaria sin comprometer la estabilidad cambiaria", dijo Felipe Barragán, estratega sénior del bróker digital Pepperstone.

* La semana pasada, el banco central mexicano sorprendió con un recorte de 25 puntos base a su tasa clave, a un 6.25%, una decisión cuestionada por analistas ante el deterioro del panorama inflacionario local, la depreciación del peso -que a inicios de septiembre se negociaba por debajo de 17 por dólar- y una economía con un desempeño mejor a lo previsto.

* Una Fed más agresiva reduciría el diferencial entre las tasas de México y Estados Unidos, erosionando aún más el atractivo de las operaciones de carry trade, que durante años han impulsado la demanda de instrumentos locales.

* La bolsa, en cambio, avanzó por sexta jornada consecutiva y terminó muy cerca de su récord máximo, según datos preliminares de cierre.

* El índice accionario líder S&P/BMV IPC .MXX subió un marginal 0.06% a 71,899.12 puntos, luego de revertir sus pérdidas iniciales, impulsada principalmente por firmas del sector aéreo.

* Los títulos de la aerolínea Volaris VOLARA.MX encabezaron las alzas, con un 3.10% más a 15.98 pesos, seguidos por los del grupo aeroportuario GAP GAPB.MX, que sumaron un 2.79% a 449.07 pesos.

* En el mercado de deuda, los rendimientos primarios de los Certificados de la Tesorería (Cetes) cayeron en la subasta semanal de valores gubernamentales, reflejando el reciente recorte de Banco de México.

* La tasa del plazo referencial a 28 días se colocó en 6.20%, 30 puntos base por debajo de su remate previo.

(Reporte de Noé Torres; editado por Adriana Barrera)

(( noe.torres@thomsonreuters.com ;))

Nov. 10 (Axis negocios) -- Grupo Aeroportuario del Pacífico (GAP), which manages 12 airports in Mexico, has updated its plans for the issuance of the new fiber E that will fund its Master Development Plan (PMD), with a revised amount and date.

The amount the company intends to raise through this vehicle has decreased from 10.2 billion to 8.432 billion pesos, reflecting a 17.3% reduction, according to the latest placement prospectus.

Meanwhile, the new date for the offering execution, originally planned for July, has been moved to November 26, so the new fiber would begin trading the following day.

"This structure allows the group to diversify its funding sources, broaden the base of investors with access to the Mexican airport sector, and optimize capital allocation at the level of concessionary companies, without incorporating a secondary sales component in the offering," the company stated in preliminary documents.

The offer will involve the sale of 400 million investment trust certificates in energy and infrastructure (CBFIs), with an individual price ranging from 20 to 21.08 pesos. At the lowest price, the resources would total 8 billion pesos.

Similarly, the total amount allocated by the fiber to acquire shares in GAP's airports has been adjusted downward by 17.4%; however, it retained the acquisition of a 4.2% stake in each of them.

In this context, the valuation of the airports, which also dropped proportionally, represents 43.5% of the current market capitalization of the airport group.

What did not change was the proportion of total resources the new fiber will dedicate to each terminal, meaning that the Guadalajara Airport, GAP's most important hub, will require just over one-third (36.8%) of the funds from the operation.

Only four properties -- the terminal in the Jalisco capital and the airports of San José del Cabo, Puerto Vallarta, and Tijuana -- will account for 88% of the funds the fiber plans to invest, while the remaining 12% will suffice to acquire shares in the other eight properties.

GAP designed the fiber as part of its financing plans for the PMD 2025-2029, which is the largest in its history and involves an investment of 52 billion pesos (approximately 2.8 billion dollars).

The PMD has already allocated 12 billion pesos in 2025 and will execute another 13 billion in 2026, with plans for the modernization of the terminals in Guadalajara and Puerto Vallarta (which will account for almost half of the total amount), as well as significant investments in Tijuana and Los Cabos (one-third of the funds).

Following the news, shares of the airport operator rose 2.5% during a session in which the S&P/BMV IPC, the most representative market index, was flat near historical highs.

GAP's shares have declined 4% so far in 2026, compared to a 13.8% drop for its competitor Grupo Aeroportuario del Sureste (Asur) and a 5.2% increase for Grupo Aeroportuario del Centro Norte (OMA). During the same period, the S&P/BMV IPC, the main market index, has risen 11.7%.

The airline industry faces a challenging environment, characterized by cautious consumer spending and the impact of rising fuel prices. Some airlines, such as Volaris, have reported particular weakness in the Mexican market.

Banco de México reported that the country's international reserves increased by 150 million dollars during the week ending on November 6, reaching a total of 257,905 million dollars.

This increase represented the largest weekly gain in the last 10 weeks. International reserves are assets managed by the central bank that help address potential external financial shocks and contribute to strengthening the country's economic stability.

Additionally, the total reserves reflected a growth of 2.4% compared to the close of 2025, equivalent to a nominal increase of 6,030 million dollars so far this year.

According to Banxico, the weekly variation was the result of changes in the valuation of the Central Institute's international assets.

Mexico ranked as the sixth country with the highest foreign direct investment (FDI), receiving $34.967 billion during the first half of the year; however, it dropped from fifth place compared to the first semester of 2026.

During the same period, the profits for foreign companies that already had investments in the country reached a historic high of $43.650 billion.

Mexico and Brazil were the only two Latin American countries on the list, which is led by the Czech Republic, the Netherlands, China, and the United States.

The increase in foreign investment was primarily driven by the manufacturing sector and the reinvestment of earnings.

At a press conference following a lunch with business leaders organized by Lide Rio at the Fairmont hotel in Copacabana , in the South Zone of the capital, early Tuesday afternoon (November 10), Douglas Ruas (PL-RJ) discussed the issue regarding a potential second round in the Rio de Janeiro elections.

When asked about his meeting with Minister Cristiano Zanin from the Supreme Federal Court (STF) concerning the action requesting a second round in the state election, Ruas stated:

"I was not a part of any of these actions. The first action requesting the annulment of Garotinho's votes was actually filed by the PSD. They achieved a victory at the TSE. The TSE granted the PSD's request and annulled Garotinho's votes. It is the first time in history that we see someone go to court, win, and then appeal that victory. That is what is happening. I am not part of it; my coalition was not involved. We contested the election, received the vote of confidence on October 4, awaited the decision of the Superior Electoral Court, which announced the results, and the elections of 2026 have already concluded across the entire nation. We are not here to comment on this type of action; we are here working, already discussing and assembling our government team to deliver the best for the state of Rio de Janeiro starting in January 2027."

In closing, Ruas also asserted that "the elections are over. In 2030, we will have another opportunity for those who wish to run, they can be affiliated with a party and seek their registrations with the Electoral Justice."

Inflation in Colombia continues to be relentless, affecting the cost of living in the country.

According to a report recently released by DANE, as of October 2026, the Consumer Price Index (CPI) recorded an annual variation of 6.30% compared to the same period in 2025, when it was 5.51%.

DANE's study confirmed that the categories of Restaurants and Hotels (9.39%), Education (7.44%), Health (7.37%), Food and Non-Alcoholic Beverages (7.31%), and Furniture, Household Items, and Ordinary Household Maintenance (6.60%) reported the highest pressures, all above the national average.

Most Significant Increases

Specific products and services that significantly contributed to the annual inflation include potatoes, which saw a price increase of 98%.

Other notable increases were in services related to co-ownership (17.14%), fresh fruits (15.90%), beef (13.31%), urban transportation (10.65%), dining in sit-down restaurants (9.47%), prepared meals outside the home (9.20%), electricity (6.92%), effective rent (5.12%), and rent (5.02%).

So far this year, this indicator increased to 5.94%, which is 1.2 points higher than last year when it was at 4.74%.

Manizales

Manizales, on the other hand, reached a rate of 5.99% over the past year, primarily impacted by Restaurants and Hotels (10.33%), Health (6.88%), and Food and Non-Alcoholic Beverages (6.87%).

Nov 10 (Reuters) - The discount on Western Canada Select crude oil to North American benchmark West Texas Intermediate futures CLc1 widened on Tuesday.

WCS for December delivery in Hardisty, Alberta, settled at $25.75 a barrel below the US benchmark WTI, compared with $25 on Monday, according to brokerage CalRock.

  • The discount on heavy Canadian crude has retreated from the blowout levels of earlier this month, in part because global freight rates — while still high — have come down since October, said Rory Johnston, founder of the Commodity Context newsletter.

  • The WCS differential at Hardisty in the first week of November reached as wide as $31 below WTI. At Houston, WCS barrels in late October hit an all-time wide discount of $23 as soaring global freight rates reduced demand for Canadian crude re-exports off the US Gulf Coast.

• Los datos del IPC de EEUU refuerzan las expectativas de una subida de tasas de la Fed en diciembre
  • El dólar se fortalece y el oro cae tras conocerse los datos
  • Las acciones de Nvidia vuelven a caer, lo que lastra a Wall Street

Actualizaciones a última hora de la tarde

Por Caroline Valetkevitch y Shashwat Chauhan

10 nov (Reuters) - Los rendimientos de los bonos del Tesoro de EEUU se dispararon y las acciones de Wall Street cayeron el martes después de que una cifra de inflación estadounidense superior a lo previsto aumentara las posibilidades de que la Reserva Federal suba las tasas de interés medio punto porcentual el próximo mes.

El dólar se apreció frente a las principales divisas, mientras que el oro sufrió una fuerte caída.

El índice de precios al consumo (IPC) de EEUU subió un 0,4 % en octubre, una cifra superior a la esperada (link), tras registrar un avance del 0,6 % en septiembre, según datos oficiales. Los economistas encuestados por Reuters habían pronosticado que el IPC subiría un 0,3 % en el mes.

Además, el IPC subyacente (link) —que excluye los precios volátiles de los alimentos y la energía y al que a menudo se denomina «inflación subyacente»— se situó en el 0,3 %, por encima del consenso del 0,2 %.

Las probabilidades de que la Fed suba las tasas (link) medio punto en su reunión de política monetaria de diciembre se dispararon tras conocerse los datos. Antes de que se publicaran los datos, el gobernador de la Fed , Christopher Waller, declaró en Londres que una lectura subyacente del 0,3 % para octubre le llevaría a considerar una subida de medio punto en la reunión de la Fed del 8 al 9 de diciembre.

Lo habitual es que la Fed suba o baje las tasas en incrementos de 25 puntos básicos.

La reciente bajada de los precios del petróleo ha contribuido a aliviar parte de las preocupaciones sobre la inflación que han estado en el punto de mira de los inversionistas desde que estalló, a finales de febrero, la guerra de EEUU e Israel contra Irán (link).

«No es solo el IPC general el que está demasiado alto, sino que la crisis del petróleo se ha filtrado en el IPC subyacente », afirmó Brian Jacobsen, estratega económico jefe de Annex Wealth Management en Menomonee Falls, Wisconsin.

«Probablemente, a la Fed le preocupa ahora más la idea de que la IA desplace a otras actividades y empuje al alza los precios. Olvídate del petróleo. La nueva preocupación de la Fed es el coste de contratar fontaneros y electricistas».

El rendimiento de los bonos estadounidenses a dos años US2YT=RR, que suele evolucionar en paralelo a las expectativas sobre las tasas de interés de la Fed, subió 18,44 puntos básicos hasta el 4,731 %. El rendimiento de los bonos de referencia estadounidenses a diez años US10YT=RR subió 12,55 puntos básicos hasta el 4,988 %.

Otro factor que lastró a Wall Street fue la fuerte caída, por segundo día consecutivo, de las acciones de Nvidia NVDA.O. Los inversionistas se mostraron preocupados por el futuro del director ejecutivo, Jensen Huang, en la empresa de semiconductores después de que esta iniciara una investigación interna sobre las acusaciones de espionaje que involucran a la empresaria china Alice Huang.

La caída de Wall Street se produjo tras un fuerte repunte el lunes. Las acciones se habían recuperado de la ola de ventas de la semana pasada , ligada a las preocupaciones por un mayor control normativo sobre la inteligencia artificial a raíz del triunfo demócrata en las elecciones de mitad de mandato de EEUU El Nasdaq .IXIC, con gran peso tecnológico, cerró el lunes con una subida del 2,7 %.

Según los datos preliminares de cierre, el S&P 500 .SPX perdió 28,46 puntos, o un 0,38 %, hasta situarse en 7.521,48 puntos, mientras que el Nasdaq Composite .IXIC cedió 185,90 puntos, o un 0,74 %, hasta los 25.067,23. El Dow Jones Industrial Average .DJI bajó 161,95 puntos, es decir, un 0,31 %, hasta situarse en 52.227,80.

El índice MSCI, que mide la evolución de las acciones a nivel mundial .MIWD00000PUS, bajó 1,30 puntos, o un 0,12 %, hasta situarse en 1.107,66.

El índice paneuropeo STOXX 600 .STOXX subió un 0,3 %.

Los informes de resultados que presentarán esta semana las empresas tecnológicas supondrán otra prueba para los mercados, ya que los inversionistas se muestran preocupados por el coste del desarrollo de la IA y su rentabilidad. Los resultados de CoreWeave CRWV.O, un barómetro de la inquietud de los inversionistas respecto a la IA, se darán a conocer tras el cierre de la sesión.

La espectacular salida a bolsa de Anthropic (link) valoró al creador del chatbot Claude en hasta 1,4 billones de dólares, una cifra ligeramente inferior a algunas expectativas iniciales, lo que supone una prueba para la confianza de Wall Street en el auge de la IA que la propia empresa ayudó a impulsar. La empresa está iniciando la gira de presentación para la venta de acciones.

CAÍDA DEL PETRÓLEO Y DEL ORO; SUBIDA DEL DÓLAR

Los precios del oro cayeron tras los datos de inflación, con el oro al contado XAU= bajando un 2,62 %, hasta los 4.030,56 dólares la onza. Eldólar se apreció.

El índice del dólar =USD, que mide la cotización del dólar frente a una cesta de divisas que incluye el yen y el euro, subió un 0,56 % hasta situarse en 102,25, mientras que el euro EUR= bajó un 0,54 % hasta situarse en 1,1162 dólares. Frente al yen japonés JPY=, el dólar se fortaleció un 0,58 % hasta situarse en 158,81.

Los precios del petróleo cerraron a la baja (link) después de que las autoridades estadounidenses restaran importancia a la necesidad de una acción militar adicional contra Irán, lo que alivió los temores de nuevas interrupciones en el suministro de Oriente Medio.

Los futuros del Brent LCOc1 cayeron 1,08 dólares, o un 1,2 %, hasta situarse en 91,49 dólares el barril. El crudo estadounidense West Texas Intermediate (WTI) CLc1 bajó 81 céntimos, o un 0,9 %, hasta situarse en 86,04 dólares. Ambos índices de referencia del crudo cerraron por segundo día consecutivo en su nivel más bajo desde el 31 de agosto.

Actualiza valores al cierre

Por Froilan Romero

SANTIAGO, 10 nov (Reuters) - Las principales monedas y bolsas de valores de América Latina cayeron el martes, tras un dato de la inflación estadounidense que estuvo por encima de lo esperado y reforzó las expectativas de un alza de tasas de la Reserva Federal en diciembre.

* El Índice de Precios al Consumidor de Estados Unidos subió un 0,4% el mes pasado, tras un avance del 0,6% en septiembre, informó la Oficina de Estadísticas Laborales (BLS) del Departamento de Trabajo. Economistas encuestados por Reuters estimaban que el IPC avanzaría un 0,3% mensual.

* Más temprano, el gobernador de la Fed Christopher Waller había señalado que la entidad debería elevar los costos de financiación a corto plazo el próximo mes, incluso si los datos oficiales muestran que la inflación se moderó el mes pasado, y añadió que se debería considerar una subida mayor, de medio punto porcentual, si empeora el panorama inflacionario.

* Otras autoridades del banco cengtral estadounidense se unierpon al coro el martes en establecer la inflación como su mayor prioridad y dejaron la puerta abierta a alzas de tasas.

* Tras el reporte, el índice dólar =USD, que compara a la divisa estadounidense frente a una canasta de seis importantes monedas, avanzaba más de un 0,5%.

* Las pérdidas fueron lideradas por el peso chileno CLP=CL, CLP=, que cayó un 1,52%, a 985,50/985,80 unidades por dólar. En tanto, el principal índice de la bolsa de comercio de Santiago, el IPSA .MMXIPSAGC, subió un leve 0,07% a 10.597,22 puntos, luego de revertir pérdidas iniciales.

* El real brasileño BRL=, se depreció un 1,46%, a 5,5863 unidades por dólar, mientras que el índice Bovespa .BVSP de la bolsa B3 de Sao Paulo cedió un 0,57%, a 171.254,97 puntos.

* El peso mexicano MXN= cotizaba cerca del cierre en 18,6185 unidades, con una pérdida del 0,49%. El principal índice accionario S&P/BMV IPC .MXX, que integran las 35 empresas más líquidas del mercado mexicano, subía un 0,18% a 71.987,23 puntos. El lunes tocó un récord máximo de 72.227,22 unidades.

* El peso colombiano COP=RR terminó con caída de un 0,92% a 3.299 unidades por dólar, en su cuarta jornada de bajas; en tanto que el índice accionario de la bolsa, el MSCI COLCAP .COLCAP, caía un 2,13% a 2.521,58 puntos cerca del cierre.

* La economía de Colombia se habría expandido un 1,55% en el tercer trimestre, un crecimiento menor frente al del mismo periodo de 2025, debido al impacto negativo del terremoto de agosto, una moderación del consumo doméstico y algunos choques de oferta, reveló el martes un sondeo de Reuters.

* La moneda peruana, el sol PEN=PDSB, se depreció un 0,12% a 3,4100/3,4130 unidades por dólar. En tanto que la Bolsa de Lima .MXNUAMPESCPGPEperdió un 1,24% a 1.450,87 puntos.

* Los inversionistas dieron "un sólido respaldo" a Perú en la colocación de bonos sostenibles por 4.500 millones de dólares, la más grande en moneda extranjera de la historia del país, dijo ministro de Economía.

* Los mercados financieros de Argentina permanecían cerrados el martes por la visita al país del papa León XIV.

(Reporte de Froilán Romero. Reporte adicional de Nelson Bocanegra en Bogotá, Noé Torres, en Ciudad de México, Hernán Nessi y Jorge Otaola en Buenos Aires.
Editado por Javier Leira)

(( Froilan.romero@thomsonreuters.com ))

• US CPI data cements December Fed rate hike bets
  • Dollar strengthens and gold falls after data
  • Nvidia stock tumbles again, weighs on Wall Street

Updates to late afternoon

By Caroline Valetkevitch and Shashwat Chauhan

Nov 10 (Reuters) - US Treasury yields jumped and Wall Street stocks fell on Tuesday after a hotter-than-anticipated US inflation reading boosted chances for a Federal Reserve interest-rate hike of half a percentage point next month.

The dollar gained against major currencies, while gold fell sharply.

The US Consumer Price Index rose 0.4% in October, which was more than expected, after advancing 0.6% in September, according to official data. Economists polled by Reuters had forecast the CPI climbing 0.3% over the month.

In addition, core CPI — which strips out volatile food and energy prices and is often referred to as "underlying inflation" — landed at 0.3%, higher than the 0.2% consensus.

Odds that the Fed may raise rates half a point at its December policy meeting jumped after the data. Before the data landed, Fed Governor Christopher Waller said in London that a core reading of 0.3% for October would prompt him to consider a half point hike at the Fed's December 8-9 meeting.

The Fed more typically hikes or cuts rates in 25 basis point increments.

Lower oil prices recently have helped ease some of the inflation concerns that have been on investors' radar since the US-Israeli war with Iran erupted at the end of February.

"It’s not just headline CPI that is too high, but the oil shock has seeped into core," said Brian Jacobsen, chief economic strategist at Annex Wealth Management in Menomonee Falls, Wisconsin.

"The Fed is probably now more concerned about the idea of AI crowding out other activity and pushing up prices. Forget about oil. The new Fed worry is the cost of hiring plumbers and electricians."

The US 2-year note US2YT=RR yield, which typically moves in step with interest rate expectations for the Fed, rose 18.44 basis points to 4.731%. The yield on benchmark US 10-year notes US10YT=RR rose 12.55 basis points to 4.988%.

Also weighing on Wall Street, Nvidia’s NVDA.O stock fell sharply for a second straight day. Investors worried about CEO Jensen Huang's future at the chip company after it initiated an internal probe into spy claims involving Chinese businesswoman Alice Huang.

Wall Street's decline followed a sharp rally on Monday. Stocks had bounced back from a selloff last week that was tied to worries about increased AI regulation in the wake of a Democratic sweep in the US midterm elections. The tech-heavy Nasdaq .IXIC closed 2.7% higher on Monday.

According to preliminary closing data, the S&P 500 .SPX lost 28.46 points, or 0.38%, to end at 7,521.48 points, while the Nasdaq Composite .IXIC lost 185.90 points, or 0.74%, to 25,067.23. The Dow Jones Industrial Average .DJI fell 161.95 points, or 0.31%, to 52,227.80.

MSCI's gauge of stocks across the globe .MIWD00000PUS fell 1.30 points, or 0.12%, to 1,107.66.

The pan-European STOXX 600 .STOXX index climbed 0.3%.

Earnings reports due this week from tech companies will be another test for markets as investors fret about the cost of the AI buildout and its profitability. Results from CoreWeave CRWV.O, a barometer of investor anxiety over AI, are due after the closing bell.

Nov 10 (Reuters) - US Treasury yields jumped and Wall Street stocks fell on Tuesday after a hotter-than-anticipated US inflation reading boosted chances for a Federal Reserve interest-rate hike of half a percentage point next month.

The dollar gained against major currencies, while gold fell sharply.

The US Consumer Price Index rose 0.4% in October, which was more than expected, after advancing 0.6% in September, according to official data. Economists polled by Reuters had forecast the CPI climbing 0.3% over the month.

In addition, core CPI — which strips out volatile food and energy prices and is often referred to as "underlying inflation" — landed at 0.3%, higher than the 0.2% consensus.

Odds that the Fed may raise rates half a point at its December policy meeting jumped after the data. Before the data landed, Fed Governor Christopher Waller said in London that a core reading of 0.3% for October would prompt him to consider a half point hike at the Fed's December 8-9 meeting.

The Fed more typically hikes or cuts rates in 25 basis point increments.

Lower oil prices recently have helped ease some of the inflation concerns that have been on investors' radar since the US-Israeli war with Iran erupted at the end of February.

"It’s not just headline CPI that is too high, but the oil shock has seeped into core," said Brian Jacobsen, chief economic strategist at Annex Wealth Management in Menomonee Falls, Wisconsin.

Nov 10, 2026

Andina Peru's agricultural exports will pass $15bn this year, Minister of Foreign Trade and Tourism Rogers Valencia said, state news agencyreported on November 9. He also said the country should turn itself into a logistics hub serving South America.

The forecast would keep Peru near the record it set in 2025, when farm shipments reached $15bn, a 17.3% rise on 2024. Growth has slowed sharply this year. Agricultural exports totalled $8.334bn between January and August 2026, up 2.3% from the same eight months of the previous year.

Valencia spoke at a ceremony marking Exporter's Day in Lima. He described the expected result as an achievement but said it was not enough. He added that the Andean and Amazonian regions must be brought further into the agricultural export value chain.

The minister said Peru's export performance had taken a great deal of effort. It rested in part on a constitution that guarantees equal treatment for exporters and for business owners, whether domestic or foreign.

Valencia named bilingualism as one challenge facing the Peruvian workforce. He pointed to China, which he said has 300mn English speakers, and argued that English should be Peru's next step.

He described logistics as another priority. Peru has spent billions of dollars on roads and ports, he said, and must now use that infrastructure to become a logistics hub. Such a role would raise domestic productivity and also serve other South American countries, he added.

The minister said Peru's National Plan to 2040 sets out a national roadmap and a model for growth in the economy. He said this progress came not only from new products and trade agreements but also from a vision covering the whole country. The next task, he added, was to open markets for other products.

Nov 10, 2026

El Economista Peru is set to replace Chile as South America's fourth-largest economy in 2027, based on International Monetary Fund (IMF) projections,reported on November 8.

La Tercera Faster growth in Peru drives the change. The IMF expects Peru to expand more quickly than its southern neighbour every year through 2031, while the two economies are now separated by only a few billion dollars. The estimates come from the fund's World Economic Outlook and were compiled by the Chilean newspaper.

The IMF forecasts Peru's gross domestic product (GDP) at $413.597bn in 2027, a fraction above the $413.443bn projected for Chile. Peru's lead would grow to $435bn against $430.4bn in 2028. By 2031, the IMF sees the Peruvian economy reaching $502bn, compared with $486.5bn for Chile.

The IMF projects Peruvian growth of 3% this year, against 0.6% for Chile. In 2027 the two countries would expand by 2.9% and 2.6% respectively. Peru would grow 3% and Chile 2.3% in 2028. In 2031 the projected rates are 3.2% for Peru and 2.4% for Chile.

Peru's GDP stood at about $342bn in 2025, while Chile's was $357.4bn. For 2026, the IMF puts Chile at $402.2bn and Peru at $399.6bn.

La Tercera reported that Peru could pull ahead even before 2027. The newspaper said Chile's economy shrank by a cumulative 0.4% between January and September 2026. Chile would need to grow 3.6% in the fourth quarter to meet the IMF's full-year forecast of 0.6%.

Brazil would remain the continent's largest economy. The IMF projects its GDP at $2.65tn this year, rising to $3.39tn in 2031. Argentina would rank second, at an estimated $768.206bn this year and $855.399bn by 2031.

Colombia would stay in third place, with GDP of $572.375bn in 2026 and a projected $762.67bn in 2031.
