Nov 10, 2026

EFE. Chile's annual inflation rate reached 4.5% in October, with fuel costs the main driver, according to the National Statistics Institute (INE), as reported by

Consumer prices rose 0.5% on the month. Of the 13 divisions inChile's truckers split over nationwide stoppage as San Antonio port dispute ends with 8% rate rise the index basket, six made a positive contribution, five a negative one and two had none, INE said.

Transport recorded the sharpest increases: fuel for private vehicles climbed 5.6% and passenger air transport 4.2%. Food and non-alcoholic beverages rose in 13 of 15 categories, led by vegetables, pulses and tubers at 4.6%, followed by bread, cereals, flours and pasta at 0.8%. Clothing and footwear moved the other way, with clothing down 3.9% and footwear down 4.7%.

Diesel, which is key to the country's logistics infrastructure, rose 12.3% over the period and is up 53.3% so far this year, INE data show. At the end of October, diesel increased by about $0.094 (CLP91.5) per litre to $1.59 (CLP1,558). Petrol of 93 and 97 octane rose $0.042 (CLP41.3) to $1.56 (CLP1,527) per litre. Fuel prices have now risen five times in a row since July, following the impact of the US-led war against Iran, and experts expect a sixth increase in the coming days.

The figures land as the government of President José Antonio Kast looks to growth. It secured approval of an economic and tax reform in early August, including corporate tax cuts, which it aims to use to lift growth to 3.5% by the end of its term. The Central Bank of Chile has cut its 2026 growth forecast to a range of 0.25% to 0.75% and warned of persistent 'inflationary risk' after its latest monetary policy meeting.

By comparison, the economy grew 2.5% in 2025 and inflation closed that year at 3.5%, its lowest in five years.

• Alice Huang facilitó envíos de chips de Nvidia por valor de al menos 7.500 millones de dólares a empresas chinas - The Information
  • Microsoft recupera brevemente el segundo puesto entre las empresas más valiosas

Añadir detalles de la rueda de prensa de Donald Trump del lunes en los párrafos 5 y 6, detalles del informe del NYT en los párrafos 7 y 8, y del informe del FT en los párrafos 19 y 20

10 nov (Reuters) - Las acciones de Nvidia NVDA.O ampliaron sus pérdidas el martes, lo que sitúa al gigante de los chips en camino de perder más de 470 000 millones de dólares en valor de mercado en dos sesiones, a medida que aumentaban las preocupaciones por las repercusiones de la relación del director ejecutivo, Jensen Huang, con una empresaria china de la que se sospecha que es espía de Pekín.

La relación del director ejecutivo con Alice Huang (link) contribuyó a facilitar el envío de chips de Nvidia por valor de al menos 7.500 millones de dólares a empresas chinas, según informó el martes The Information (link), citando a dos personas que la conocen. Alice Huang y Jensen Huang no tienen parentesco alguno.

El consejo de administración de Nvidia inició una investigación interna el domingo, y sus consejeros independientes anunciaron el martes que habían contratado al exfiscal federal en funciones Joon Kim y al bufete de abogados Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz para dirigir la investigación de la empresa.

Por su parte, el FBI está investigando por separado si Huang, de 63 años, fue objeto de una operación de inteligencia extranjera (link). Huang ha confesado a sus empleados que fue infiel a su esposa, pero no ha dado detalles sobre la relación.

El presidente Donald Trump declaró el lunes (link) que había hablado con Huang y le había preguntado si sabía que la mujer era, supuestamente, una espía china. Trump afirmó que Huang le había dicho que «no tenía ni la más remota idea» y que creía al director ejecutivo de Nvidia.

Trump también afirmó que no tenía conocimiento de los supuestos vínculos cuando Huang le acompañó a China en mayo.

Sin embargo, el «New York Times» informó el martes de que el secretario de Estado y asesor de seguridad nacional, Marco Rubio, había informado a Trump a bordo del Air Force One, de camino a China, sobre datos de los servicios de inteligencia estadounidenses que indicaban que Huang mantenía una relación con una mujer de la que se creía que era una espía china.

Según el NYT , que citaba a personas con conocimiento del asunto, esta reunión informativa supuso al menos la segunda vez en siete meses que se informaba a Trump sobre esos datos de inteligencia.

Las acusaciones han intensificado el escrutinio sobre la gobernanza de Nvidia, el cumplimiento de las normas de control de exportaciones y la dependencia del liderazgo de Huang (link), lo que se suma a la inquietud de los inversionistas sobre si el gasto masivo en infraestructura de inteligencia artificial generará una rentabilidad adecuada.

Las acciones de Nvidia cayeron más de un 6 % tras un descenso del 4,3 % el lunes, lo que permitió a Microsoft MSFT.O superar brevemente a la empresa líder en IA como la segunda empresa más valiosa del mundo por primera vez desde junio de 2025.

«El debate en torno a la inversión gira en torno a si esto sigue siendo un asunto específico de la empresa o si desencadenará restricciones y trastornos en toda la infraestructura de IA», escribieron los analistas de Bank of America en una nota. «No equipararíamos las acusaciones con un perjuicio empresarial demostrado».

Alice Huang, también conocida como Huang Le, junto con su marido y su hermana, creó una red de empresas en China y Singapur para adquirir chips de Nvidia, según informó The Information.

En el centro de la red se encontraba Shanghái Century Litong, una empresa con sede en China que consiguió en 2023 la condición de socio preferente en la nube de Nvidia, lo que le otorgaba acceso prioritario a los chips de la empresa, según el informe.

Cuando se estancaron los pedidos de chips de Nvidia sujetos a restricciones de exportación de EEUU, Alice Huang utilizó sus vínculos con Nvidia y sus distribuidores para garantizar el suministro, lo que contribuyó a introducir en China unos 240 000 chips H100, H200 y algunos A100, según el informe.

Alibaba, Tencent, Megaspeed y Shanghái Century Litong no estuvieron disponibles de inmediato para hacer declaraciones fuera del horario laboral habitual. • Microsoft recupera brevemente el segundo puesto entre las empresas más valiosas

lseg:urn:newsml:reuters.com:20261110:nL6.html_limpio:
• Alice Huang facilitated at least $7.5 billion of Nvidia chip shipments to Chinese firms - The Information
  • Microsoft briefly retakes the second-most valuable company spot

Add details from Donald Trump's briefing on Monday in paragraphs 5,6, details from NYT report in paragraphs 7,8 and the FT report in paragraphs 19,20

Nov 10 (Reuters) - Nvidia NVDA.O shares extended losses on Tuesday, putting the chip giant on track to shed more than $470 billion in market value over two sessions as concerns mounted over the fallout from CEO Jensen Huang's affair with a Chinese businesswoman alleged to be a spy for Beijing.

The CEO's relationship with Alice Huang helped facilitate shipments of at least $7.5 billion worth of Nvidia chips to Chinese firms, The Information reported on Tuesday, citing two people who know her. Alice Huang and Jensen Huang are not related.

Nvidia's board launched an internal investigation on Sunday, and its independent directors on Tuesday said they had retained former acting US Attorney Joon Kim and law firm Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz to lead the company's investigation.

The FBI is separately examining whether the 63-year-old Huang was targeted by a foreign intelligence operation. Huang has told employees he was unfaithful to his wife but provided no details about the relationship.

President Donald Trump said on Monday he had spoken with Huang and asked whether he knew the woman was allegedly a Chinese spy. Trump said Huang told him he had "absolutely no idea" and that he believed the Nvidia CEO.

Trump also said he had not known about the alleged ties when Huang accompanied him to China in May.

However, the New York Times reported on Tuesday that Secretary of State and national security adviser Marco Rubio had briefed Trump aboard Air Force One en route to China about US intelligence indicating Huang was involved with a woman believed to be a Chinese spy.

The briefing marked at least the second time in seven months that Trump had been told about the intelligence, the NYT reported, citing people with knowledge of the matter.

The allegations have intensified scrutiny of Nvidia's governance, export-control compliance and reliance on Huang's leadership, adding to investor unease over whether massive spending on artificial intelligence infrastructure will deliver adequate returns.

Nvidia's shares fell more than 6% following a 4.3% drop on Monday, allowing Microsoft MSFT.O to briefly overtake the AI bellwether as the world's second-most valuable company for the first time since June 2025.

"The investment debate is whether this remains company-specific or triggers restrictions and disruption across AI infrastructure," Bank of America analysts wrote in a note. "We would not equate allegations with proven business damage."

Alice Huang, also known as Huang Le, along with her husband and sister, built a network of companies across China and Singapore to acquire Nvidia chips, The Information reported.

At the center of the network was Shanghai Century Litong, a China-based company that secured preferred cloud partner status with Nvidia in 2023, giving it priority access to the company's chips, the report said.

When orders for Nvidia chips subject to US export restrictions stalled, Alice Huang used ties to Nvidia and its distributors to secure supplies, helping move about 240,000 H100, H200 and some A100 chips into China, according to the report.

Century Litong rented computing capacity and operated data centers using Nvidia chips, including some barred from sale to China. Some of the chips ultimately served Alibaba 9988.HK, Tencent 0700.HK and smaller Chinese AI labs, The Information reported.

Alice Huang also held an executive position at Singapore-registered Megaspeed, which was linked to Century Litong and has been investigated by US authorities over Nvidia chip shipments from Southeast Asia to China, the report said.

The Information also reported that Alice Huang leveraged her relationship with Jensen Huang to bolster her credibility while keeping her role vague and avoiding a paper trail.

Meanwhile, the US commerce department is delaying efforts to blacklist Megaspeed, the Financial Times reported, citing people familiar with the deliberations.

The Commerce Department, which chairs the government panel overseeing a so-called entity list of groups connected to China that allegedly posed national security risks, had sought more information about some companies under consideration, the FT reported.

It was unclear whether Megaspeed was among those companies, but the delay has left it off the list, according to the report.

The US Department of Commerce and Nvidia did not immediately respond to Reuters requests for comment. Alibaba, Tencent, Megaspeed and Shanghai Century Litong were not immediately available for comment outside regular business hours. Reuters could not independently verify the reports.

(Reporting by Anhata Rooprai in Bengaluru, and Steve Holland and Humeyra Pamuk in Washington; Editing by Anil D'Silva and Leroy Leo)

(( Anhata.Rooprai@thomsonreuters.com ))

Por Noel Randewich y Chuck Mikolajczak

NUEVA YORK, 10 nov (Reuters) - Las acciones tecnológicas volvieron a cerrar en rojo este martes, ya que los pasos de Anthropic hacia una gran salida a bolsa no lograron calmar la inquietud generalizada sobre la salud del sector de la inteligencia artificial.

Las ventas se vieron impulsadas por un informe sobre la inflación en EEUU que apuntaba a cifras elevadas (link), lo que aumentó las expectativas de que la Reserva Federal vuelva a subir las tasas de interés el próximo mes, junto con la noticia de que Nvidia NVDA.O ha contratado a abogados para llevar a cabo una investigación interna (link) relacionada con su director ejecutivo y el hecho de que el desarrollo de un centro de datos en Ohio (link) se está complicando cada vez más.

Muchos inversores se mantuvieron optimistas sobre las perspectivas de las inversiones en IA, aunque reconocieron que la volatilidad se ha convertido en una realidad del mercado este otoño. El índice Nasdaq Composite .IXIC bajó un 1 % el martes por la tarde. Durante el último mes, el índice ha caído un 1 % o más en ocho ocasiones y ha subido un 1 % o más en seis ocasiones.

«Existe preocupación por lo que ocurre en la cúpula de Nvidia y, si es sustituido, por quién lo sustituirá», afirmó Tim Ghriskey, estratega sénior de carteras de Ingalls & Snyder en Nueva York, quien señaló que considera las ventas en Nvidia y otras grandes empresas de IA como oportunidades de compra. «Pero no veo que Nvidia se vaya a desmoronar. Veo una empresa muy sólida afectada por algo ajeno a su control».

Además de Nvidia, que bajó un 6,5 %, las principales caídas se registraron sobre todo entre las grandes beneficiarias del repunte de la IA que arrasó en los mercados durante las dos primeras terceras partes de este año. El fabricante de servidores Dell Technologies DELL.N bajó un 4,8 % el martes, pero acumula una subida del 161 % en lo que va de año, según datos de LSEG, mientras que la empresa de chips Sandisk SNDK.O bajó un 4,5 % en la jornada y acumula una subida del 257 % en lo que va de año.

Entre las «neoclouds» —pequeñas empresas de infraestructura de IA que han estado bajo presión este mes debido a las preocupaciones sobre su capacidad para recaudar fondos en unas condiciones de mercado más restrictivas—, Iren IREN.O cayó un 10 %, Nebius NBIS.O bajó un 7 % y CoreWeave CRWV.O retrocedió un 3 %. Las tres han caído al menos un 40 % desde que el Nasdaq alcanzara su máximo más reciente el 6 de octubre. CoreWeave tiene previsto publicar sus resultados tras el cierre del martes.

Muchos inversores afirmaron que, en su opinión, la inquietud generalizada del mercado estaba detrás de gran parte de las ventas, a pesar de que fue una jornada repleta de noticias sobre temas relacionados con la IA. El proveedor británico de servicios en la nube Nscale está barajando la posibilidad de retrasar su salida a bolsa, valorada en 35 000 millones de dólares (link), según informó The Telegraph el martes.

Las acciones del fabricante de equipos eléctricos GE Vernova GEV.N cayeron más de un 6 % el martes, después de que la firma de inversión japonesa SoftBank 9984.T revisara sus planes de adquisición de equipos para sus proyectos de centros de datos en EEUU GE Vernova es una de las empresas que participan en el desarrollo de la colosal central eléctrica de gas y el centro de datos de SoftBank en el condado de Pike, Ohio, según indicaron los analistas.

Nvidia NVDA.O estaba a punto de perder más de 470 000 millones de dólares (link) en valor de mercado en dos sesiones, a medida que aumentaba la preocupación por las repercusiones del romance del director ejecutivo Jensen Huang con una empresaria china de la que se sospecha que es espía de Pekín.

Aun así, los inversores se centraban principalmente en la perspectiva a largo plazo.

«Siempre podemos atribuir una razón a por qué las cosas están más volátiles. Y sin duda han estado más volátiles en las últimas semanas, desde octubre, digamos», afirmó Jason Ware, director de inversiones de Albion Financial Group en Salt Lake City, Utah. «Pero, al fin y al cabo, la trayectoria de las acciones en las próximas semanas y meses va a depender realmente de los resultados».

Tras el informe sobre la inflación del martes, muchos inversores centrarán su atención en los próximos grandes acontecimientos para las acciones tecnológicas, que serán la publicación de resultados de Nvidia tras el cierre de la bolsa dentro de una semana y la salida a bolsa de Anthropic en los días posteriores, independientemente de cómo se comporten las acciones en un día concreto.

«Probablemente volveremos a tener beneficios récord el año que viene, a menos que se produzca una recesión o un cambio radical en la inversión en IA, y no espero que ocurra ninguna de las dos cosas», afirmó Ware, cuya empresa tiene en cartera acciones de Nvidia. «Por eso creo que la señal la marcará la trayectoria de los beneficios y un crecimiento económico superior al 2 %. Y el resto no es más que ruido a corto plazo que, como he dicho, se irá disipando con el tiempo».

By Noel Randewich and Chuck Mikolajczak

NEW YORK, Nov 10 (Reuters) - Technology shares were in the red again on Tuesday, with Anthropic's steps toward a big IPO failing to calm general anxiety about the health of the AI sector.

Selling was driven by a hot US inflation report that increased expectations the Federal Reserve will raise rates again next month, alongside Nvidia's NVDA.Ohiring lawyers for an internal investigation tied to its CEO and the development of an Ohio data center getting more complicated.

Many investors remained optimistic about the prospects for AI investments while allowing that volatility has become a fact of market life this fall. The Nasdaq Composite .IXIC was off 1% on Tuesday afternoon. Over the past month, the index has dropped by 1% or more eight times and risen by 1% or more six times.

"There is concern about what happens at the top at Nvidia, and if he's replaced, who's he replaced with," said Tim Ghriskey, senior portfolio strategist at Ingalls & Snyder in New York, who said he sees selling in Nvidia and other major AI firms as buying opportunities. "But I don’t see Nvidia falling apart. I see a very strong company hit by something not of its own making."

Besides Nvidia, down 6.5%, the major decliners were mostly big beneficiaries of the AI rally that swept markets for the first two-thirds of this year. Server maker Dell Technologies DELL.N was down 4.8% on Tuesday but up 161% for the year, according to LSEG data, while chip firm Sandisk SNDK.O was down 4.5% for the day and up 257% for the year.

Among the neoclouds, smaller AI infrastructure firms that have been under pressure this month amid concerns about their capacity to raise funds under tighter market conditions, Iren IREN.O dropped 10%, Nebius NBIS.O fell 7% and CoreWeave CRWV.O slid 3%. All three have declined by at least 40% since the Nasdaq hit its most recent high on October 6. CoreWeave is due to report earnings after the close on Tuesday.

Many investors said they thought general market anxiety was behind much of the selling, despite a newsy day across AI-related subjects. British cloud services provider Nscale is considering delaying a $35 billion stock market listing, The Telegraph reported on Tuesday.

Shares of power equipment maker GE Vernova GEV.N slid more than 6% on Tuesday, after Japanese investment firm SoftBank 9984.T revised equipment procurement plans for its US data center projects. GE Vernova is among the companies involved in the development of SoftBank's colossal gas-fired power plant and data center in Pike County, Ohio, analysts said.

Nvidia’s NVDA.O was on track to shed more than $470 billion in market value over two sessions as concerns mounted over the fallout from CEO Jensen Huang's affair with a Chinese businesswoman alleged to be a spy for Beijing.

Even so, investors were mostly focused on the longer-term picture.

"We can always ascribe a reason as to why things are more volatile. And they have been more volatile the last few weeks for sure, since October, let's call it," said Jason Ware, chief investment officer at Albion Financial Group in Salt Lake City, Utah. "But at the end of the day, the path for stocks over the coming weeks and months is going to be really a story of earnings."

Following Tuesday’s inflation report, many investors will be focusing on the next big events for technology stocks, which stand to be Nvidia’s earnings report after the close a week from today and Anthropic’s IPO in the days after, regardless of what stocks do on a given day.

“We're probably gonna have record earnings again next year unless we see a recession or a massive pivoting on AI capex, and I don't expect either one,” said Ware, whose firm owns Nvidia. “And so I think that's going to be the signal is the trajectory of earnings, the economy growing more than 2%. And the rest of this is sort of just short-term noise that will, like I said, get ironed out over time."

(Reporting by Noel Randewich and Chuck Mikolajczak, editing by Colin Barr and Nick Zieminski)

Añade detalles sobre las posibles obligaciones del consejero delegado en virtud del código de conducta de la empresa y actualiza la cotización de las acciones

  • Varios consejeros forman parte del consejo de administración desde la década de los noventa
  • La empresa se compromete a llevar a cabo una investigación exhaustiva
  • Se insta al consejo de administración a recabar asesoramiento jurídico independiente

Por Ross Kerber

10 nov (Reuters) - Las revelaciones de que el director ejecutivo de Nvidia NVDA.O, Jensen Huang, mantuvo una relación extramatrimonial con una empresaria (link), sospechosa de ser una espía china, han obligado al consejo de administración del fabricante de chips a enfrentarse a algo más que una simple conducta indebida por parte de un ejecutivo, lo que plantea cuestiones existenciales para la empresa y dudas sobre la capacidad del consejo para investigar a su director ejecutivo de forma independiente.

Entre los líderes empresariales, «sin duda ha habido escándalos de aventuras amorosas y de acoso sexual. ¿Pero escándalos de “trampas amorosas”? No», afirmó Ann Lipton, profesora de Derecho de la Universidad de Colorado que sigue de cerca los asuntos relacionados con los consejos de administración.

Lipton utilizaba un término que hace referencia a una estratagema de espionaje en la que un agente atrapa a su objetivo fingiendo interés romántico. Entre los ejemplos históricos se encuentra el «caso Profumo» (link) a principios de la década de 1960, y suelen acarrear consecuencias diplomáticas o políticas.

El presidente de EEUU, Donald Trump (link), afirmó el lunes que el FBI está investigando la relación de Huang, un día después de que el consejo de administración de Nvidia iniciara una investigación interna «en relación con las preocupaciones de seguridad nacional planteadas en las noticias (link) », según un correo electrónico que Huang envió a los empleados de Nvidia y que la empresa hizo público.

Hay mucho en juego. Aunque no está claro si Huang infringió el código de conducta de la empresa (link) ni a qué sanciones podría enfrentarse, sus estatutos (link) permiten su destitución «con o sin causa» mediante el voto de la mayoría de los consejeros.

Los semiconductores avanzados de la empresa se encuentran en el centro de una carrera mundial por la supremacía en inteligencia artificial. El Ministerio de Asuntos Exteriores de China calificó la acusación de espionaje de «acusación infundada, calumnia y difamación».

Huang, cofundador de Nvidia, de 63 años, no tiene un sucesor claro, además de mantener estrechos vínculos con Trump. Huang posee el 3,6 % de las acciones de Nvidia y tiene docenas de subordinados directos, lo que sugiere un control férreo sobre la empresa.

Las acciones de Nvidia NVDA.O bajaron un 6 % el martes, ampliando así las pérdidas (link) registradas el lunes a raíz de las repercusiones del escándalo de Huang.

LA CREDIBILIDAD DEL CONSEJO

A diferencia de lo que suele ser habitual entre sus competidores, Nvidia opera sin un presidente del consejo entre sus 11 consejeros. Aunque la empresa considera independientes a todos menos a Huang, tres consejeros independientes llevan en el cargo desde la década de los noventa y un cuarto, Mark Stevens, durante la mayor parte de ese tiempo. Solo dos se han incorporado al consejo desde 2021.

Esta lista de miembros, con un carácter casi de club, quizá no resulte tan inusual si se compara con los estándares de los carismáticos fundadores de empresas de Silicon Valley, como Steve Jobs, de Apple, fallecido en 2011.

Pero la investigación estadounidense ha intensificado el escrutinio sobre si los consejeros que han trabajado junto a Huang durante décadas son lo suficientemente independientes como para investigar su conducta.

«Si se trata de una figura como Steve Jobs, creo que tanto en Wall Street como en Silicon Valley se diría que tiene derecho a cierto margen de maniobra o deferencia», afirmó Marc Goldstein, director de investigación en EEUU de la consultora de voto Institutional Shareholder Services.

Esa deferencia podría ahora plantear dudas sobre si el consejo de administración ejerció una supervisión suficiente sobre un director ejecutivo cuyo propio criterio ha sido objeto de escrutinio.

Nvidia declaró el domingo que, aunque su consejo no tiene motivos para creer que se hayan visto comprometidos ni la seguridad nacional de EEUU ni los secretos de Nvidia, su investigación examinaría toda la información disponible (link). El consejo afirmó que tiene confianza en el director ejecutivo y en su equipo directivo.

Goldstein señaló que los miembros del consejo que llevan a cabo esa investigación deberían tener libertad para contratar a sus propios asesores jurídicos con el fin de reforzar su credibilidad. La empresa también podría considerar mantener a los consejeros con más antigüedad al margen de la investigación, añadió Goldstein, para evitar impugnaciones legales por parte de accionistas que aleguen que no fue lo suficientemente independiente.

ASUNTO JURÍDICO

Un factor que deberá tener en cuenta el consejo es si Huang informó a la empresa de la relación. El código de conducta de Nvidia incluye las «relaciones personales» entre los tipos de actividades que pueden generar conflictos de intereses para los empleados, junto con actividades como aceptar trabajos de consultoría externos, ocupar puestos en consejos de administración o desempeñar funciones de asesoramiento.

«Si te ves involucrado en una situación que pudiera suponer un conflicto de intereses, ya sea real o aparente, ponte en contacto con el departamento jurídico de Recursos Humanos para recibir orientación», reza el documento.

Gil Soffer, antiguo funcionario del Departamento de Justicia de EEUU y actual presidente del bufete de abogados Katten, afirmó por correo electrónico que una revelación completa y precisa por parte de Huang sería favorable para su situación actual, ya que «significaría que no ocultó la relación y que, presumiblemente, el consejo tuvo la oportunidad de evaluar la misma, establecer medidas de protección y gestionar de otro modo el posible conflicto».

Soffer señaló que se necesitan más datos públicos para saber si, de hecho, la relación generó un conflicto, si la junta directiva ha actuado adecuadamente hasta ahora o qué sanción, si la hubiera, podría estar justificada para Huang.

En un escenario desfavorable, como que Huang hubiera ocultado la relación y cometido una conducta indebida, «la destitución podría ser adecuada», afirmó Soffer.

Huang percibió 120 millones de dólares en los últimos tres años, según muestra el último informe de representación de la empresa, en su mayor parte a través de concesiones de acciones. El documento afirma: «Nuestros directivos son empleados “a voluntad” y no tenemos acuerdos laborales, de indemnización por despido ni de cambio de control con ellos».

ECONOMÍA POLÍTICA

Jeffrey Sonnenfeld, profesor de gestión de la Universidad de Yale, señaló que la empresa se enfrenta a cuestiones adicionales de seguridad nacional debido a los vínculos (link) entre Huang y Trump. Trump, que ha elogiado a Huang, declaró el lunes que había hablado con el director ejecutivo y que creía que «estaría bien».

Estados Unidos ha impuesto restricciones a las exportaciones de chips avanzados de IA a China desde 2022. El año pasado (link) la Administración Trump permitió a Nvidia reanudar determinados envíos a China en virtud de acuerdos por los que el Gobierno estadounidense recibe una parte de las ventas de chips de la empresa en ese país.

Este acuerdo hace que cualquier insinuación de espionaje extranjero resulte más delicada tanto para los ejecutivos como para los funcionarios del Gobierno de EEUU, señaló Sonnenfeld.

«Por eso no conviene que haya acuerdos de capitalismo de Estado. No conviene que el Gobierno de EEUU se involucre tanto en las empresas privadas», afirmó Sonnenfeld.

Adds details on CEO's potential obligations under company code of conduct, updates share price

  • Several directors have been on the board since the 1990s
  • Company vows to conduct a thorough investigation
  • Board is urged to enlist independent legal advice

By Ross Kerber

Nov 10 (Reuters) - Revelations that Nvidia NVDA.O Chief Executive Jensen Huang had an affair with a businesswoman suspected of being a Chinese spy have forced the chipmaker's board to confront more than ordinary executive misconduct, raising existential questions for the company and concerns about the board's ability to investigate its CEO independently.

Among corporate leaders, "There have definitely been affair scandals and sexual-harassment scandals. But honey-pot scandals? No," said Ann Lipton, a University of Colorado law professor who follows boardroom issues.

Lipton was using a term for an espionage ploy in which an operative entraps a target by feigning romantic interest. Historical examples include the Profumo Affair in the early 1960s and tend to involve diplomatic or political consequences.

US President Donald Trump said on Monday the FBI is investigating Huang's relationship, a day after Nvidia's board launched an internal investigation "regarding the national security concerns raised in news reports," according to an email Huang sent to Nvidia employees and released by the company.

The stakes are high. While it is not clear if Huang violated the company's code of conduct or what penalties Huang could face, its bylaws allow his removal "with or without cause" by the vote of a majority of directors.

The company's advanced semiconductors are at the heart of a global race for AI superiority. China's Foreign Ministry called the spying claim "a groundless accusation, slander and a smear."

Nvidia co-founder Huang, 63, has no obvious successor, as well as close ties to Trump. Huang owns 3.6% of Nvidia's stock and has dozens of direct reports, suggesting a tight grip on the company.

Shares in Nvidia NVDA.O were down 6% on Tuesday, extending their losses from Monday over fallout from Huang's affair.

BOARD'S CREDIBILITY

Unusually among its peers, Nvidia operates without a board chair among its 11 directors. While the company considers all but Huang independent, three independent directors have served since the 1990s and a fourth, Mark Stevens, for most of that time. Only two have joined the board since 2021.

The clubby roster may not be so unusual by the standards of charismatic Silicon Valley company founders like Apple's Steve Jobs, who died in 2011.

But the US probe has heightened scrutiny of whether directors who have worked alongside Huang for decades are sufficiently independent to investigate his conduct.

"If you have a figure like Steve Jobs, I think people on Wall Street as well as in Silicon Valley would say they're entitled to some leeway or deference," said Marc Goldstein, head of US research for proxy adviser Institutional Shareholder Services.

Such deference could now raise questions about whether the board provided sufficient oversight of a CEO whose own judgment has come under scrutiny.

Nvidia said on Sunday that while its board has no reason to believe that either US national security or Nvidia secrets were compromised, its inquiry would examine all available information. The board said it has confidence in the CEO and his leadership team.

Goldstein said board members running that investigation should be given the latitude to hire their own legal advisers to bolster their credibility. The company also might consider keeping long-serving directors away from the probe, Goldstein added, to avoid legal challenges from shareholders claiming it wasn't sufficiently independent.

A factor for the board to consider will be whether Huang reported the affair to the company. Nvidia's code of conduct lists "personal relationships" among the types of activities that may create conflicts of interest for employees, along with activities like taking on outside consulting work, board seats or advisory roles.

"If involved in a situation that could present a perceived or actual conflict of interest, contact Employment Legal for guidance," the document states.

Gil Soffer, a former US Justice Department official and now chair of law firm Katten, said via email a complete and accurate disclosure by Huang would be favorable for his situation now since it "would mean he didn't conceal the relationship, and that the board presumably had the opportunity to evaluate the relationship, set up guardrails and otherwise manage the potential conflict."

Soffer said more public facts are needed to know whether a conflict was in fact created by the relationship, whether the board acted appropriately so far, or what if any punishment of Huang might be justified.

In a bad scenario such as Huang concealing the relationship and engaging in misconduct, "removal could be appropriate," Soffer said.

Huang was paid $120 million over the past three years, the company's latest proxy shows, largely through stock awards. The document states, "Our executive officers are 'at-will' employees and we do not have employment, severance or change-in-control agreements with our executive officers."

Yale University management professor Jeffrey Sonnenfeld said the company faces additional national-security questions because of the ties between Huang and Trump. Trump, who has praised Huang, said on Monday that he had spoken to the CEO and thought he would "be in good shape."

The United States has imposed restrictions on exports of advanced AI chips to China since 2022. Last year the Trump administration allowed Nvidia to resume certain China shipments under arrangements in which the US government receives a cut of the company's China chip sales.

The deal makes any suggestion of foreign espionage more sensitive for both executives and US government officials, Sonnenfeld said.

"That's why you don't want state capitalism arrangements. You don't want the US government to be so involved in private companies," Sonnenfeld said.

Among corporate leaders, "There have definitely been affair scandals and sexual-harassment scandals. But honey-pot scandals? No," said Ann Lipton, a University of Colorado law professor who follows boardroom issues.

The average price of roasted chicken in Colombia was $43,703 in October, reflecting an annual increase of 6.78%, according to measurements from the Roasted Chicken Index (IPA).

This figure was reported following the National Administrative Department of Statistics (Dane) announcement that the national annual inflation rate stood at 6.30% in the tenth month of the year.

According to the report, five spending categories exceeded the national average in October: recreation and culture (0.44%), housing, water, electricity, gas, and other fuels (0.30%), health (0.26%), clothing and footwear (0.24%), and finally, restaurants and hotels (0.23%).

The price adjustment for the dish, which cost $40,928 in October 2025, was attributed to the direct impact of utility rates, labor costs, rental fees for commercial spaces, and operational supplies on businesses.

In terms of city pricing, Medellín registered the highest cost in the country, with an average of $52,670 per unit, representing an annual increase of 18.42%. In Villavicencio, the price reached $44,800, while in Bogotá it was $44,520. In contrast, Cali reported an average price of $40,900, and Tunja had the lowest figure at $36,450.

Regarding the cost structure of raw materials, Nicolás Cruz Walteros, a local economic analyst at Corficolombiana, noted that "while an increase in chicken supply was observed, it does not mean that the input is free from cost increases, particularly due to the price fluctuations of feed ingredients such as corn and soy, which are essential for poultry production."

Furthermore, poultry meat as an input showed a monthly negative variation of 0.30% and an annual increase of 3.43%, indicating that the rise in prepared product prices concentrated in restaurant operations.

In this regard, Valentina Guio, head of Macroeconomic Studies at the National Association of Financial Institutions (Anif), stated that "other costs, such as labor, utility services, and rent, have driven prices upward."

Corficolombiana and financial institutions project that food and meals outside the home will continue to face pressure due to climatic factors associated with the El Niño phenomenon and the impact of the minimum wage on the sector's payroll.

Colombians are expected to face the most expensive Christmas of the last three years this December. Analysts project that annual inflation will close 2026 between 6.7% and 6.9%, the highest level since 2023 when the indicator surpassed 9%, according to data from the National Administrative Department of Statistics (DANE).

This increase in costs does not stem from a single cause. Behind the rising prices are higher labor costs, adjustments of goods and services tied to past inflation, and utility rates.

On top of these pressures is the possibility that the El Niño phenomenon will affect food production and increase energy and gas costs.

In practice, households will feel the impact on purchases for family dinners, dining out, gifts, and other expenses typical of the holiday season.

December Inflation Will Range Between 6.7% and 6.9%

José Luis Mojica, manager of Macroeconomic Research at Bancolombia, projects that annual inflation will reach 6.7% by the end of 2026. He added that one of the main factors behind price variations throughout the year is indexation, which refers to price adjustments referencing inflation in previous periods.

This is compounded by a 23.7% increase in the minimum wage for 2026, which has pressured costs across various economic activities and translated into higher prices for certain goods and services.

"This would basically result from the continuation of the effects we've seen this year in indexation, which has led to annual adjustments in several components of the basket that have internalized both increasingly higher levels of inflation and the unprecedented increase of the minimum wage we had for 2026 at 23.7%," Mojica noted.

Aval Asset Management's projection is slightly higher. Juan David Ballén, director of Economic Studies at the firm, estimates the Consumer Price Index (CPI) will close December 2026 at 6.9%.

For Ballén, the persistence of price increases in services and regulated industries will be determinative. These increases are related to higher labor costs, adjustments based on past inflation, and changes in utility rates.

However, the analyst notes that the appreciation of the Colombian peso has moderated the cost of some imported goods.

What Will Be Expensive This Christmas

Mojica warned that December has seasonal characteristics that can intensify price pressures. During this month, there is an increase in year-end purchases, consumption of gift-related goods, and demand for services associated with celebrations.

In particular, he anticipates higher pressures on entertainment and other activities that typically see price increases during the holiday season.

"The highest inflation pressures will be concentrated in core inflation, particularly in goods and services, which at this time of year contribute most to monthly results," he explained.

For Ballén, price variations will be particularly felt in food intended for family dinners, restaurants, and other services related to celebrations. Therefore, even though inflation would be below the peaks recorded in 2022 and 2023, the budget necessary for the festivities would be greater than last year.

How Will the El Niño Phenomenon Affect Christmas Costs?

Analysts are warning about the risks associated with the El Niño phenomenon. Its intensity and the effects of droughts represent an uncertain variable but could serve as an additional source of price increases.

Consult: Six Months of Rising Costs for Food, Energy, and Gas Ahead

Mojica indicated that weather conditions would affect both food and energy and gas rates. In the first case, challenges in production and supply would drive up prices for items reaching households. In the second, the conditions of the energy system could create additional pressures on rates.

This concern is relevant for December because food typically experiences a seasonal upward trend during this month. If this trend is compounded by climate impacts, purchases for family gatherings would be more expensive.

Inflation is Already at 6.30%

Year-end projections come after the cost of living has remained above 6% for five consecutive months. In October, the CPI registered an annual variation of 6.30% compared to the same month in 2025, according to DANE.

The result was driven by increases in restaurants and hotels, education, health, and food, four categories that exceeded the national average.

Restaurants and hotels had the highest annual variation at 9.39%. They were followed by education at 7.44%; health at 7.37%; food and non-alcoholic beverages at 7.31%; and furniture, household items, and ordinary household maintenance at 6.60%.

These figures indicate that several categories with significant everyday expenses were already experiencing increases above the national average before the holiday season.

Additionally, inflation is still far from the Banco de la República's target of 3%. This upward trend contrasts with what occurred after 2023 when the indicator began to decline.

10 nov (Reuters) - Nscale, un proveedor británico de servicios en la nube respaldado por el gigante de los chips Nvidia NVDA.O, está barajando la posibilidad de retrasar su salida a bolsa, valorada en 35 000 millones de dólares, según informó el martes el diario The Telegraph .

Los directivos de esta empresa dedicada al desarrollo de centros de datos están valorando si suspender los preparativos para salir a bolsa hasta el año que viene, añade el informe.

Nscale no respondió de inmediato a una solicitud de comentarios de Reuters fuera del horario laboral habitual.

La noticia se produce pocos días después de que Reuters informara de que Microsoft MSFT.O había rechazado (link) una opción para ampliar su acuerdo existente con Nscale con el fin de alquilar más potencia de cálculo en un centro de datos de Texas.

La empresa, con sede en Londres, presentó una solicitud de salida a bolsa en septiembre, cuando buscaba una financiación de unos (link) 3.5 mil millones de dólares, incluidos 2 mil millones de dólares de Nvidia.

Nscale tiene previsto cotizar (link) en la Bolsa de Nueva York (NYSE) con el símbolo «NSCL».

La noticia sobre la salida a bolsa de Nscalellega en un momento en queAnthropic sigue adelante con sus propios planes de cotización. El gigante de la IA presentó el martes un folleto actualizado para su salida a bolsa, en el que busca una valoración de hasta 1,4 billones de dólares (link), ligeramente por debajo de las expectativas de algunos inversores.

La salida a bolsa de Anthropic se considera una prueba clave de la confianza de Wall Street en el auge de la IA que ella misma ayudó a impulsar.

lseg:urn:newsml:reuters.com:20261110:nL6.html_limpio:
Adds details and background from paragraph 3 onwards

Nov 10 (Reuters) - Nscale, a British cloud provider backed by chip giant Nvidia NVDA.O, is considering delaying a $35 billion stock market listing, the Telegraph reported on Tuesday.

Executives at the data-centre developer are assessing whether to pause efforts to go public until next year, the report added.

Nscale did not immediately respond to a Reuters request for comment outside regular business hours.

The report comes days after Reuters reported that Microsoft MSFT.O had declined an option to expand its existing agreement with Nscale to rent more computing power at a Texas data center.

The London-based company filed for an IPO in September, when it sought about $3.5 billion in funding, including $2 billion from Nvidia.

Nscale plans to list on the NYSE under the symbol "NSCL."

The news about Nscale's IPOcomes asAnthropic moves ahead with its own listing plans. The AI giant on Tuesday filed an updated prospectus for its IPO, seeking a valuation of up to $1.4 trillion, slightly short of some investors' expectations.

Anthropic's IPO is seen as a key test of Wall Street's faith in the AI boom it helped ignite.

(Reporting by Sumedha Mukherjee in Bengaluru; Editing by Jonathan Ananda and Leroy Leo)

(( Sumedha.Mukherjee2@thomsonreuters.com ))

During an event hosted by the presidency of COP31 on Tuesday (10) in Antalya, André Corrêa do Lago, the president of COP30, led the proceedings. He reintroduced the roadmap for transitioning away from fossil fuels while the host nation, Turkey, celebrated the discovery of new oil wells in the country.

On what was termed "energy day" at the conference, a unified discourse surrounding renewable sources featured prominent environmental leaders, including Marina Silva and John Kerry, while Brazilian NGOs highlighted that Petrobras secured over $60 billion in financing since the signing of the Paris Agreement.

The former Minister of the Environment and a standout figure at the event received a standing ovation when she spoke about the reelection of President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT). She made the "L" gesture with her hand, a symbol that is gaining international recognition, but she also issued a warning about a forthcoming contradiction that the Lula administration must contend with.

"Electrification is a concrete opportunity, but we need to ask: electrify with what energy? Its climate potential depends on the expansion, clean generation of networks, storage, and efficiency," she noted.

Electrification is a key priority for the Turkish presidency of the COP, which is shared this year with Australia, striving for a goal of 35% electrification by 2035 without explicitly stating that this milestone should be achieved using clean energy.

According to observers, Brazil would support the measure without reservations. This stance is not based on self-interest, given that its energy matrix is mostly clean, but rather for diplomatic reasons, as a target focused solely on renewables would be complex for other countries.

Lula arrived in Antalya early in the morning and had only one engagement for the day— a closed-door meeting with his Turkish counterpart, Recep Tayyip Erdogan. He is already facing the ambiguity of having led the energy transition proposal in Belém last year while also promoting oil exploration in the Equatorial Margin.

He managed to secure only one voluntary proposal, reintroduced in this edition and bolstered by the surprising victory in the October election and four consecutive years of declining deforestation. At the leaders' meeting, which begins on Wednesday, it will undoubtedly be one of the major attractions.

However, he will continue to be tied to the label of being described as a hero of environmentalism while simultaneously advocating for the exploration of new oil wells at the mouth of the Amazon.

"Brazil's initiative to encourage other countries to develop their roadmaps for moving away from fossil fuels is commendable, but it contradicts what is happening in the country," asserts Suely Araújo, public policy coordinator at the Climate Observatory.

"The document approved by the National Energy Policy Council, which has not yet been published, currently limits itself to a list of 18 guidelines that will not change the reality in this domain. Brazil needs to establish a strong commitment to decarbonization, with goals and timelines, and this is far from happening."

A report released on Tuesday by the NGO in collaboration with Stand.Earth, ClimaInfo, and WWF-Brasil indicates that Petrobras raised $61.5 billion in funding from major banks since the signing of the Paris Agreement.

Regarding the exploration of new fields, the expected investment is $42 billion by 2040, when global oil consumption is projected to decline, according to the International Energy Agency.

"The report makes it clear the risks of financing oil production expansion, especially in sensitive areas. There is a lot of contradiction in the current scenario, a bit of schizophrenia. Fossil fuels are being greatly expanded alongside a narrative of transition," the environmentalist stated.

The organizations are urging banks, both national and international, to halt financing for the oil industry, aligning with what the Brazilian government advocates for other countries during the COP.

Kerry, the former U.S. Secretary of State and another prominent figure in global environmentalism, declared that the energy transition "is what the world desires." Proof of this, according to him, was seen in the midterm elections in the U.S., which represented a resounding defeat for the denialist administration of Donald Trump.

"I am proud to be here a week after we have regained common sense," Kerry said, receiving applause akin to Marina's.

At the close of trading, the euro was quoted at 1,098.27 Chilean pesos , representing an increase of 1.17% compared to the previous closing price of 1,085.57 Chilean pesos. Source: Dow Jones.

Over the past week, the euro has registered a gain of 1.2%, while its year-on-year variation stands at an increase of 6.11% .

The euro to Chilean peso exchange rate has shown a positive trend over the last day. Current volatility stands at 14.38%, significantly above the reference volatility of 9.93%, indicating an unstable scenario in the foreign exchange market.

The Journey of the Chilean Peso

The Chilean peso has been the legal tender of Chile since 1975, reverting to the peso symbol ($) and is regulated by the Central Bank of Chile, which controls the amount of money created.

The Chilean currency was established in 1817 following the country's independence, but it wasn't until 1851 that the decimal system was implemented in the Chilean peso, which is now composed of 100 centavos. Over time, the currency has undergone changes, but it is currently counted in whole pesos.

As of now, coins worth 5, 10, 50, 100, and 500 pesos are available; the latter was the first bimetallic coin produced in the country. In 2009, there was an attempt to introduce 20 and 200 peso coins, but the project was rejected by Congress. Meanwhile, in 2017, it was approved to cease the issuance of 1 and 5 peso coins.

Additionally, in October 2018, the Central Bank of Chile announced that it would begin withdrawing from circulation the 100 peso coins created between 1981 and 2000, in order to reduce their coexistence with current coins, although they remain valid.

In terms of economic matters, Chile had a strong fiscal response in 2021, enabling it to grow by up to 11.7%, making it one of the fastest recoveries in the world following the coronavirus pandemic. This situation can be explained by consumption driven by the withdrawal of pension funds and direct fiscal support.

Despite this, the recovery in the labor market has been slower, and inflation has also affected Chile, fueled by strong demand pressures, rising commodity prices, supply disruptions, and the depreciation of the peso, which ultimately led to the highest public debt in three decades (37%).

• Los legisladores quieren reuniones informativas con Huang y las agencias de inteligencia
  • Schumer y Jeffries afirman que esta cuestión obliga al Congreso a aprobar rápidamente nuevas restricciones a las exportaciones de chips estadounidenses a China
  • Schumer afirma que Trump debe explicar su defensa de Huang

Se añaden más detalles y antecedentes; no hay comentarios inmediatos de la Casa Blanca ni de Nvidia en los párrafos 3 a 12

Por David Shepardson y Courtney Rozen

WASHINGTON, 10 nov (Reuters) - El líder demócrata del Senado, Chuck Schumer, afirmó el martes que el Congreso debe obtener una explicación exhaustiva sobre la defensa que el presidente Donald Trump ha hecho del director ejecutivo de Nvidia NVDA.O, Jensen Huang, y pidió a los legisladores que aprueben rápidamente nuevas restricciones a las exportaciones de chips estadounidenses a China.

Schumer citó informes según los cuales Trump fue informado hace un año de la relación de Huang con una presunta espía china y no hizo nada al respecto.

«Menudo incumplimiento del deber. Se supone que debe proteger a Estados Unidos, no a China, ni a sus amigos. Trump se ha dedicado a intentar defender a Jensen Huang cuando debería estar defendiendo nuestra seguridad nacional», afirmó Schumer. «Necesitamos una explicación exhaustiva sobre la inacción de Trump a la hora de hacer frente al espionaje extranjero en la industria tecnológica estadounidense».

Ni la Casa Blanca ni Nvidia respondieron de inmediato a las solicitudes de comentarios. Un número cada vez mayor de legisladores quiere que se impongan restricciones a las exportaciones estadounidenses de chips a China como parte de un proyecto de ley anual de defensa.

«Esta alarmante situación deja claro que el Congreso debe actuar ahora para aprobar una legislación bipartidista fundamental… con el fin de cortar el acceso de China a la tecnología avanzada estadounidense antes de que sea demasiado tarde», afirmó Schumer.

La versión del Senado del proyecto de ley de defensa contiene disposiciones paraotorgar al Congreso más autoridad sobre los chips de IA destinados a China, instar a los aliados de EEUU a restringir las ventas de equipos de fabricación de semiconductores a China y exigir a las empresas que realicen un seguimiento de sus chips de IA en el extranjero para combatir el contrabando.

Los legisladores quieren que Huang les informe al respecto.

El senador demócrata Rubén Gallego declaró: «Nvidia ha estado solicitando permiso para vender chips avanzados a China. Necesitamos saber en qué medida la espía china influyó en la decisión del director ejecutivo Jensen».

Trump declaró el lunes que había hablado con Huang, quien le dijo que no tenía ni idea de que la mujer fuera una espía. Trump añadió que estaba «asombrado» por las acusaciones y que el FBI estaba investigando el asunto.

El consejo de administración de Nvidia inició una investigación después de que el *New York Times* revelara que Huang mantenía una estrecha relación con una empresaria china que, según creen los servicios de inteligencia estadounidenses, compartía información con Pekín.

«Una de nuestras empresas más importantes, dedicada a la seguridad nacional, cuyo director ejecutivo podría estar manteniendo una relación con una espía china, y Trump no hizo nada al respecto», afirmó Schumer.

Señaló que Trump invitó a Huang a acompañarle en una visita a Pekín y aceptó una donación de 25 millones de dólares de la empresa para el salón de baile de la Casa Blanca.

«También necesitamos respuestas sobre la campaña de influencia de Nvidia y cómo afectó a las decisiones de seguridad nacional de la Administración Trump, incluida la flexibilización —la flexibilización— de controles clave a la exportación», afirmó Schumer.

Huang es uno de los aliados más cercanos de Trump en Silicon Valley, y la relación entre ambos se remonta, como mínimo, a 2025.

En los últimos dos años, ha expresado en repetidas ocasiones su apoyo a la agenda de la Administración y se ha convertido en una presencia habitual en Washington, mientras Nvidia intentaba vender chips avanzados al mercado chino.

The people of the Falkland Islands face "devastating consequences" if Argentina is successful in blocking development of its offshore oilfield, the attorney general for England and Wales has told an international tribunal.

Ellie Reeves, representing the British government at a hearing of the international tribunal for the law of the sea (Itlos), said billions of pounds vital to the future of the British overseas territory would be lost.

Reeves accused Argentina of surreptitiously seeking to pursue its longstanding sovereignty claims over the south Atlantic islands through an application to the tribunal, which is sitting over two days in Hamburg.

Argentina is seeking a provisional ruling suspending the drilling for oil before further arbitration over the future of the project, which it claims poses an environmental risk.

Reeves told the tribunal: "In reality, what Argentina opposes is hydrocarbon activities for the economic benefit of the Falkland Islanders. What it wants is to take control of those resources for itself."

Argentina claims Britain's approval of the Sea Lion project is in breach of a 1976 UN resolution calling on both parties to desist from unilateral action on the islands until the sovereignty dispute is settled.

Buenos Aires wants to force a commitment from the UK that it will "stop the drilling", in order to "preserve the present situation" before a settlement over the oilfield.

After raising Argentina's "armed invasion" of the islands in 1982, which she told the tribunal led to "loss of life and military occupation", Reeves said the Falkland Islanders had a right to exploit their own natural resources, adding that a tribunal that ruled over the law of the seas had no place in settling a sovereignty dispute.

Reeves said that suspension of the drilling, which is due to start in March next year, would kill off the Sea Lion project.

"The provisional measures sought by Argentina would prevent the people of the Falkland Islands from developing their natural resources as they are entitled to do so, pursuant to their fundamental right to self-determination," she said.

"The measures sought would have devastating consequences for the Falklands people. They risk losing billions of pounds in money, which is essential for the islands' economic development."

Sir Michael Wood KC, who also spoke on behalf of the UK, said the tribunal could lose member states should it overreach by issuing "provisional" measures that should be used only in exceptional circumstances.

Asked whether the UK would abide by the tribunal's ruling, Reeves told the Guardian that she respected the institution but that she would not "get ahead" of the decisions.

Speaking earlier on Tuesday, Mario Oyarzábal, chief legal adviser to Argentina's ministry of foreign affairs, had told the tribunal that the 3,600 inhabitants of the Falkland Islands, had no right to the resources around the south Atlantic archipelago.

Oyarzábal said: "[Argentina] respects the interests of the inhabitants of the islands and their way of life as enshrined in the Argentine constitution … What these British citizens do not have is a right to decide to which state the islands belong …

"These resources belong to the Argentine people. Some 46 million of them including the 1,247 inhabitants born on the islands whose interests will be duly taken into account."

He said Argentina was ready to negotiate "all aspects of the question" of the Falkland Islands, which are known as the Malvinas in Argentina, "including the present aggravation of the dispute caused by the UK".

He accused the UK of refusing to enter talks over the islands while pushing forward on the exploitation of its natural resources in a way that would entrench the status quo.

Oyarzábal claimed that the oil money from the drilling would "finance the very military base and presence that sustains the UK's de facto control of the territory".

Argentina's case is that provisional measures to suspend the drilling are urgent. The Sea Lion project in the North Falkland basin, led by the Israeli firm Navitas and its British partner, Rockhopper, will start drilling in March and oil will be extracted from 2028 and continue for 35 years. It has the potential to double the islands' GDP per capita to a cumulative uplift of £8bn over the lifetime of the project. The UK government asked why an application to Itlos had only been made in recent months amid increasingly bellicose rhetoric.

Argentina further claims that it has rights as the "coastal state" to the Falklands. The UK's lawyers said this claim highlighted that Argentina's application was "at heart" about sovereignty.

The Sea Lion project has been condemned as unlawful by Argentina's president, Javier Milei. The tribunal was told by Argentinian lawyers that the permissions given by the UK government for drilling was the "unilateral conduct" of a "colonial power".

Oyarzábal added: "In the event of a blowout or spill, it is Argentina that would bear its consequences and be called upon to respond, not a state that is 12,700km away."

UK lawyers responded that the risk of such an incident was low and that the companies involved had mitigated against it.

Argentina invaded the Falklands in 1982 at the cost of the lives of 649 Argentinian military personnel, 255 British military personnel and three Falkland Islanders. The hearing is the first time that substantive matters relating to the islands have been litigated at an international tribunal. In a show of solidarity, Princess Anne arrived in Port Stanley on Monday. The hearing continues on Wednesday.

• Lawmakers want briefings with Huang, intelligence agencies
  • Schumer, Jeffries say issue means Congress must quickly pass new restrictions on US chips exports to China
  • Schumer says Trump must explain defense of Huang

Adds more details, background, no immediate White House and Nvidia comments in paragraphs 3-12

By David Shepardson and Courtney Rozen

WASHINGTON, Nov 10 (Reuters) - Senate Democratic Leader Chuck Schumer on Tuesday said Congress must have a full accounting of President Donald Trump's defense of Nvidia NVDA.O CEO Jensen Huang and called on lawmakers to quickly approve new restrictions on US chip exports to China.

Schumer cited reports Trump was briefed on Huang’s affair with a suspected Chinese spy a year ago and did nothing.

"What a dereliction of duty. He’s supposed to protect America, not China, not his friends. Trump has been busy trying to defend Jensen Huang when he ought to be defending our national security," Schumer said. "We need a full accounting for Trump’s failure to address foreign espionage in the American tech industry."

The White House and Nvidia did not immediately respond to requests for comment. A growing number of lawmakers want restrictions on US exports of chips to China as part of an annual defense bill.

"This alarming situation makes it clear that Congress must act now to pass critical bipartisan legislation ... to cut off China’s access to advanced American technology before it’s too late," Schumer said.

A Senate version of the defense bill contains provisions to giving Congress more authority on AI chips going to China, prodding US allies to restrict sales of semiconductor manufacturing equipment to China and requiring businesses to track their AI chips abroad to combat smuggling.

Lawmakers want a briefing with Huang.

Democratic Senator Ruben Gallego said, "Nvidia has been asking permission to sell advanced chips to China. We need to know how much the Chinese spy influenced CEO Jensen’s decision."

Trump said Monday he had spoken to Huang, who told him that he had no idea that the woman was a spy. Trump added he was "amazed" by the allegations and that the FBI was now looking into the issue.

Nvidia's board launched a probe after the New York Times said Huang ⁠had a close relationship with a Chinese businesswoman who US intelligence officials believe shared information with Beijing.

"One of our most important companies that is involved in national security, and the CEO might be having an affair with a Chinese spy, and Trump did nothing about it," Schumer said.

He noted that Trump invited Huang to join him on a visit to Beijing and accepted a $25 million donation from the company for his White House ballroom.

"We also need answers on Nvidia’s influence campaign and how it affected the Trump administration’s national security decisions, including the loosening – the loosening – of key export controls," Schumer said.

Huang is one of Trump's closest allies in Silicon Valley, and the relationship between the two dates ⁠to at least 2025.

Over the past two years, he has repeatedly voiced support for the administration's agenda and become ⁠a regular presence in Washington as Nvidia sought to sell advanced chips to the Chinese market.

(Reporting by David Shepardson; Editing by Alistair Bell)

(( David.Shepardson@thomsonreuters.com ; 2028988324; ))

"One of our most important companies that is involved in national security, and the CEO might be having an affair with a Chinese spy, and Trump did nothing about it," Schumer said.

He noted that Trump invited Huang to join him on a visit to Beijing and accepted a $25 million donation from the company for his White House ballroom.

"We also need answers on Nvidia’s influence campaign and how it affected the Trump administration’s national security decisions, including the loosening – the loosening – of key export controls," Schumer said.

Huang is one of Trump's closest allies in Silicon Valley, and the relationship between the two dates ⁠to at least 2025.

Over the past two years, he has repeatedly voiced support for the administration's agenda and become ⁠a regular presence in Washington as Nvidia sought to sell advanced chips to the Chinese market.

• Colombia October inflation edges up to 6.3%
  • Colombia third-quarter economic growth seen cooling - poll
  • Brazilian real briefly touches lowest level in 15 months
  • Traders pricing in two 25-basis-point Fed rate hikes by March

Updates with afternoon trading

By Ragini Mathur, Sudeshna Ghoshal and Avinash P

Nov 10 (Reuters) - An index tracking Latin American currencies fell to a seven-month low on Tuesday after a hotter-than-expected US inflation report reinforced expectations that the Federal Reserve will raise interest rates next month, lifting the dollar and dimming the appeal of emerging-market assets.

MSCI's Latin American currency index .MILA00000CUS fell 0.8%, touching its lowest level since April in intraday trading. A gauge of regional equities .MILA00000PUS dropped 1.3%.

The dollar =USD strengthened 0.6% against a basket of major currencies and Treasury yields rallied after data showed US consumer prices rose more than expected in October. Traders are now fully pricing in two 25-basis-point Fed rate hikes by March, according to LSEG data.

A stronger dollar and rising US Treasury yields typically weigh on emerging markets by drawing capital toward US assets, weakening the demand for riskier developing market assets.

An earlier risk-on mood, initially supported by lower oil prices, faded after the inflation data. The US-Israeli war on Iran has lifted and kept oil prices elevated this year, complicating the inflation and interest-rate outlooks for central banks worldwide.

In Brazil, the equity benchmark fell 0.5%, while the real BRL=briefly touched its weakest level since August 2025 at 5.6133 a dollar. It was last down 1.4%.

Brazilian assets have sold off sharply since President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva's reelection in October.

Brazil's central bank said worsening inflation prospects, despite slowing growth, reflected four supply shocks: higher oil prices, El Niño-related pressures, the end of the 44-hour work week and a weaker currency driven by domestic policy uncertainty.

The assessment came in minutes from last week's policy meeting, when officials halted their easing cycle and held the benchmark Selic rate at 13.75%.

"The minutes reinforced the message of the post-meeting statement that the inflation scenario has worsened. However, weaker economic activity and the already very high degree of monetary tightening suggest that there is no need to raise interest rates, at least for now," said Caio Megale, chief economist at XP, in a note.

In Colombia, the stock index .COLCAP fell 2.2%, while the peso COP= edged 0.8% lower to its weakest level in over a month.

Data released late on Monday showed consumer prices rose 0.2% in October from September, slowing from a 0.37% increase in September. Annual inflation, however, inched up to 6.3% from 6.29%. The data comes as President Abelardo de la Espriella's government faces mounting fiscal pressure.

Meanwhile, Colombia's economy likely slowed in the third quarter, weighed by a deadly August earthquake, a dip in domestic consumption and supply shocks, a Reuters poll showed.

Mexican shares .MXX inched 0.1% higher and were on track for a sixth straight day of gains, their longest streak since December 2025. The peso MXN= was down 0.45%.

Por Marcela Ayres

BRASILIA, 10 nov (Reuters) - El presidente del Banco Central de Brasil, Gabriel Galípolo, dijo el martes que el organismo utilizaría una política monetaria restrictiva para mantener la inflación bajo control, aunque ello provocara tensiones en otros sectores de la economía.

Sus declaraciones ocurrieron horas después de que los analistas interpretaran de forma generalizada las minutas de la última reunión de política monetaria del banco central como de sesgo expansivo y reforzó las expectativas de que el umbral para nuevas subidas de tasas sigue siendo alto, a pesar del deterioro de las perspectivas de inflación.

La semana pasada, el banco suspendió el ciclo de relajación monetaria que había iniciado en marzo, manteniendo la tasa de referencia Selic en el 13,75%. Las promesas de gasto del presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva y su reelección el mes pasado han provocado un fuerte debilitamiento del real brasileño BRBY y también han impulsado las tasas de interés a largo plazo.

En las minutas, los responsables de la política monetaria argumentaron que el deterioro de las perspectivas de inflación reflejaba perturbaciones del lado de la oferta y señalaron que una desaceleración económica más acusada podría ayudar a limitar los efectos de arrastre más amplios sobre los precios al consumidor.

En un acto celebrado en São Paulo, Galípolo dijo que las elevadas tasas de interés a largo plazo reflejan factores que escapan al control del Banco Central.

Señaló que la demanda de títulos públicos indexados a la tasa Selic, que representan más de la mitad de la deuda pública de Brasil, se basa, en última instancia, en la confianza de los inversionistas en que el Banco Central subirá las tasas de interés siempre que sea necesario para combatir la inflación.

"Eso es lo que el banco central ha hecho históricamente y seguirá haciendo", dijo.

Galípolo añadió que la reticencia de los inversionistas a mantener bonos indexados a la inflación apunta a preocupaciones que van más allá de la tasa de interés oficial y que se reflejan en la curva de rendimientos en su conjunto.

Recurriendo a una analogía médica, reconoció que las tasas de interés elevadas pueden tener efectos secundarios adversos, pero dijo que el Banco Central seguirá dando prioridad a la estabilidad de precios.

"El Banco Central seguirá prescribiendo el mismo tratamiento. Se administrará el medicamento, incluso en dosis elevadas", dijo.

Galípolo también señaló que la emisión de deuda en moneda local, tal y como hace Brasil en la mayor parte de su endeudamiento, otorga al Estado una mayor flexibilidad, pero hace que sean los inversionistas quienes asuman los riesgos.

(Reporte de Marcela Ayres; edición de Fernando Cardosoen Español de Manuel Farías)

(( marcela.ayres@thomsonreuters.com ; +55 11 5047-2444; ))

Press Release article 3 of 3, Source: WEC, 313 words

Nov 18, 2025: ASUR SIGNS DEAL TO ACQUIRE MOTIVA'S STAKE IN AIRPORT BUSINESS IN BRAZIL, ECUADOR, COSTA RICA AND CURACAO

Grupo Aeroportuario del Sureste, S.A.B. de C.V. (NYSE:ASR; BMV:ASUR) ("ASUR") and Motiva Infraestrutura de Mobilidade S.A. (B3: MOTV3) ("Motiva") today announced that ASUR has entered into a purchase agreement with Motiva to acquire all of the issued and outstanding equity interest of Companhia de Participacoes em Concessoes ("CPC"), a wholly owned subsidiary of Motiva, for a purchase price of R$5,000 million (US$936 million)1,2, with an implied enterprise value R$13,700 million (US$2,566 million) 2,3. CPC owns equity interests in 20 airports with concessions in Brazil, Ecuador, Costa Rica and Curacao. The portfolio includes the Quito International Airport in Quito, Ecuador, the Juan Santamaria International Airport in San Jose, Costa Rica, the Curacao International Airport in Curacao, the Confins International Airport in Brazil, as well as the Pampulha airport, the Bloco Sul airports, and the Bloco Central airports in Brazil. The portfolio reported EBITDA for the twelve- month period ending September 30, 2025, on an 100% basis, of R$2,000 million (US$375 million 2 ) and, on a proportionate basis to CPC's stake, of R$1,300 million (US$243 million 2 ); and, net financial debt as of September 30, 2025, on an 100% basis, of R$6,300 million (US$1,180 million 2 ). The acquisition represents a stepping stone in ASUR's expansion strategy in the region adding 4 new markets in Latin America and the Caribbean, including Latin America's largest aviation market by passengers, Brazil, to ASUR's existing presence in Mexico, Colombia and Puerto Rico. This acquisition will add more than 45 million passengers to ASUR's 71 million reported in 2024, consolidating ASUR as the leading airport operator in the Americas. Out of the 20 airports in CPC's portfolio, 17 have more than 15 years remaining in their concession life.

8.1 Activities

Grupo Aeroportuario del Sureste S.A. de C.V. (ASUR) is a prominent Mexican airport operator, managing a portfolio of 10 airports in the southeastern region, including the high-traffic Cancun International Airport. Its core business involves the operation, maintenance, and development of airport infrastructure, encompassing passenger and cargo handling, commercial concessions, and ancillary services like retail and parking. ASUR focuses on enhancing efficiency and passenger experience to support growing aviation demand. The company's fastest-growing segments include international passenger traffic, fueled by tourism in destinations such as Cancun and the Riviera Maya, as well as non-aeronautical revenues from expanded retail and food services, which have seen robust increases due to rising traveler spending and airport expansions. This strategic emphasis has solidified ASUR's role in Mexico's aviation industry, contributing to economic connectivity and regional development. It is the International Depository Receipt (IDR) market's 11th largest Airlines company by market capitalization.

Nov 18, 2025: ASUR SIGNS DEAL TO ACQUIRE MOTIVA'S STAKE IN AIRPORT BUSINESS IN BRAZIL, ECUADOR, COSTA RICA AND CURACAO

Grupo Aeroportuario del Sureste, S.A.B. de C.V. (NYSE:ASR; BMV:ASUR) ("ASUR") and Motiva Infraestrutura de Mobilidade S.A. (B3: MOTV3) ("Motiva") today announced that ASUR has entered into a purchase agreement with Motiva to acquire all of the issued and outstanding equity interest of Companhia de Participacoes em Concessoes ("CPC"), a wholly owned subsidiary of Motiva, for a purchase price of R$5,000 million (US$936 million)1,2, with an implied enterprise value R$13,700 million (US$2,566 million) 2,3. CPC owns equity interests in 20 airports with concessions in Brazil, Ecuador, Costa Rica and Curacao. The portfolio includes the Quito International Airport in Quito, Ecuador, the Juan Santamaria International Airport in San Jose, Costa Rica, the Curacao International Airport in Curacao, the Confins International Airport in Brazil, as well as the Pampulha airport, the Bloco Sul airports, and the Bloco Central airports in Brazil. The portfolio reported EBITDA for the twelve- month period ending September 30, 2025, on an 100% basis, of R$2,000 million (US$375 million 2 ) and, on a proportionate basis to CPC's stake, of R$1,300 million (US$243 million 2 ); and, net financial debt as of September 30, 2025, on an 100% basis, of R$6,300 million (US$1,180 million 2 ). The acquisition represents a stepping stone in ASUR's expansion strategy in the region adding 4 new markets in Latin America and the Caribbean, including Latin America's largest aviation market by passengers, Brazil, to ASUR's existing presence in Mexico, Colombia and Puerto Rico. This acquisition will add more than 45 million passengers to ASUR's 71 million reported in 2024, consolidating ASUR as the leading airport operator in the Americas. Out of the 20 airports in CPC's portfolio, 17 have more than 15 years remaining in their concession life.

Despite operating in a mature and competitive consumer staples industry, Coca-Cola FEMSA's current market valuation suggests that investors may be overlooking its resilient cash flows and strong profitability. The company's extensive distribution network and established brand portfolio provide a competitive edge, enabling it to generate recurring cash flow.

The firm maintains a strong free cash flow of about MXN 24.2 billion, showcasing its capability to support dividends, investments, and strategic acquisitions.

The company's financial health is further illustrated by its balance sheet, which lists total assets at approximately MXN 314.5 billion and total liabilities at around MXN 160.5 billion, resulting in a solid shareholders' equity of about MXN 154.0 billion. Despite slight increases in leverage due to acquisitions, Coca-Cola FEMSA continues to exhibit strong cash generation, enabling it to navigate macroeconomic challenges such as currency volatility and inflation.

While market concerns such as slowing consumer spending and rising commodity costs persist, Coca-Cola FEMSA's fundamentals remain compelling. The company manages operations spanning manufacturing, warehousing, logistics, and last-mile delivery to retailers, restaurants, and other points of sale.

This strategic approach allows the company to combine globally recognized brands with local knowledge of consumer preferences and retail formats.

Beyond classic colas, Coca-Cola Femsa manages a broad beverage portfolio that typically includes flavored sparkling soft drinks, still juices, sports drinks, teas, and bottled water. Packaging innovation plays a central role in Coca-Cola Femsa's operations, as the company strives to meet sustainability expectations and improve efficiency.

From an investor perspective, Coca-Cola Femsa is often viewed as a consumer staples business with exposure to multiple Latin American currencies and macroeconomic environments. Analysts closely monitor capital expenditure commitments, leverage metrics, and dividend policies when assessing the balance between growth investment and shareholder returns.
